Payments now say what they are for: the rent book quotes the last payment's words, and finance's books give the year's payments by what they said they were for (the nearest its papers come to a line).
- **The lending office's "signed, principal not paid out": the reader was right, the lender's memory was wrong.** The lender's code knew a loan it had offered only by the id its making gave back. The mock in a seat says each act as a seat would and hears no id, so it remembered none and paid out nothing: 232 loans offered and no principal in 120 days of the 3,000-person town. A real model in the seat would not have had the fault (it pays by its own hand), but every mock run with a lending seat did. The lender now reads its own offered loans from its file (as whoever next holds the office must). A code-run bank is unchanged.
- **Wave 2's logs and the staff-post fault** (all of `runs/w2-*` but `w2-15` read for records of kind `direction`; a subagent's scan, not checked by hand). No direction given by a model seat was lost. Five directions fell to an office whose staff were a post of their own, all `works_collection`, all from a code-run mayor, all "collect every 7 days", which is the staff's own rhythm, so nothing observable differs: w2-33-works (days 16 and 18), w2-41-works (day 15), w2-42-townworks (day 19), w2-46-largest-works (day 17). No `rates_recovery` direction was given in any pilot. Directions in pilots where the works office was run by code (w2-04, 12, 13, 27, 48, 52, 53, 58) and every staffing direction were read as they should be. So wave 2's data need no correction for this fault.
- **Limits.** Each office's reader restates what its module works out, from the same papers: a change to a module must be made in its reader (the landlord's and the support office's are held to their code twins in a run; the others by tests on papers made by hand, and not yet by a run with their office seated and busy). A mock seat's brain is the office's code, which does not read the books: what a model does with them is for the next pilot to show. The possession stages in the landlord's, the tribunal's and the registrar's books are held by tests on papers made by hand, not yet by a run in which a tenancy goes the whole way with those offices seated.
## 2026-10-11 · Founding and words: people start things of their own, and a model may write what they are for

Step 3 of the living world (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 10k). Behaviour: docs/behaviour/founding.md. The plan was put to the coordinator before the build and approved with three notes (below).

- **What was asked.** The owner: "a living breathing world"; people who have lost something "do... things"; no list of verbs. Founding in code from the blocks that exist; the words of what is founded written by a large model, asked as an author, who may decline (VISION 15, point 7); the lineage of every idea; dials; proof it is not a story generator.
- **One module, four shapes, no new word for the kernel.** A founded thing is an organisation with its founder in its first post (`group.founded`), a statement of what it is for, a gathering, an offer of membership, and for some a hearing. A group that gathers, a fund, a body that takes grievances up and a business are compositions of those; which is a parameter. *Alternatives:* a module a shape (ruled out: four copies of taking members in and lapsing); letting a founded thing publish any block (ruled out for now: nothing would say what its post does next; the shapes are what code can carry on).
- **The occasion is a want with nothing left to try, known to be shared.** Given up, or with nothing the person can see that would answer it; shared by at least two others as the person knows them (their household, what was said catching up, who told them they were wronged, who mourns the same death, who lives in the same building), **one at least from beyond the household**. The first build counted the household alone, and the pieces showed what that made: people founding a group the day someone they live with was let go, with nobody but their own family. A household alone is not others.
- **Whether and what shape are the mind's odds, drawn on the person's stream.** The chance is the profile's, swayed symmetrically by openness and achievement, care for others, the sense of agency, length of residence and ties; the shape by what the want is about and the person's values. Every size but the chance is a placeholder, named in the page.
- **The rate is anchored to registered associations, and the anchor is weak.** New registered associations run at 9 to 30 per 100,000 residents a year in the places with a figure (Victoria 29, Germany 16, England and Wales 9 for charities, the United States 30; opened). Most groups never register, and nobody counts those: `informal_multiple` is 5, a guess. `chance_bps` is fitted for Victoria's town to their product (about 1.5 new groups a year in 1,000 people): 420, over about 27 occasions a year (three runs: 21, 23, 36). The other eight profiles' chances are that one scaled by their registered rate and are not fitted. Nothing was found for congregations, tenants' associations or savings groups as rates.
- **Where a group meets is physics, then a paper.** Its founder's home, which holds so many; people beyond that are turned away at the door, which they already remember as a slight. A group that outgrows it and whose dues can carry the hire books the town's hall: a booking addressed to the town, which its works office has among its papers, and a standing payment. (The coordinator's third note: the payment should reach whoever keeps the hall as an ordinary paper a steward can see. It does; nobody grants or refuses one yet, and the world's own groups still use the hall for nothing: for a later step.) The first rule let a fund book the hall whenever it had three evenings' hire in the bank, and funds spent their members' dues on a room: now its dues between gatherings must come to the hire.
- **Joining is the matching that already exists.** A standing offer of membership is an opening read for what it brings in typed outcomes and whom it bears on; the union's application and membership agreement carry it. One statement kind is newly published for it (`membership`), in a town with founding on. **Found:** a fund is joined for bringing "money to me" whatever the sum, so a fund asking a few minutes' pay a month gathers a hundred members in a year where a circle gathers five. The matching is blind to size, as step 2's was built; it is a limit to read runs by, not changed here.
- **The composing model: an author shown a record, who may decline** (VISION 15, point 7; the prompt is in docs/behaviour/founding.md and `participants/src/llm/compose.ts`, version 0.1.0). One call a piece; the record shown once; nothing kept by the model. It is shown the founder's own record and nobody else's, in words code renders. *Not done, and it would need a stop first:* giving it the person's earlier pieces, or asking it to continue as them.
- **Nothing a model writes reaches the world except through a layer that can only choose or copy** (the coordinator's first note). A piece's four parts go through the translator as plain requests; a code person cannot read a preview, so the module that asked says what the draft may be (`accept`), and the orchestrator carries out only what that returns. What the translator cannot write arrives as the composer's closed choice among the options the request listed, written by code; failing that, the plain default. Which way each part arrived is recorded. *Alternative ruled out:* code reading the composer's fields directly and skipping the translator (the words of entities are traffic the translator must learn, and its failures on them are the finding).
- **What the translators made of it** (a code-seat year, 13 foundings; `runs/living-world-3-2026-10-11/words-1`): the name and the statement of purpose went through 13 of 13 each, written by the trained translator in front (`decide/pod-small-r2-s1`). The gathering and the offer of membership went through 0 of 13: the trained one's drafts were not what was meant, and the prompt-driven one behind (`claude-code/claude-sonnet-5-5`) wrote the gathering as a paper put up at a place ("a lot, or a cell") and the offer as an agreement ("An agreement with whom?"). Neither has ever been shown a statement carrying a practice or an offer as data. All 26 arrived as closed choices. The translator's prompt was not touched. **For the translator's next round:** these 52 requests, and the two shapes they need.
- **Softening, measured, on one family** (`runs/living-world-3-2026-10-11/audit-1`; 12 recorded situations, 6 dark; `claude-code/claude-sonnet-5-5`; Codex's window was shut all day, so there is no second family and no second judge yet: the audit serves what it has from its file when run again). Declined: 0 of 40. By the word counts, against ten real texts: hope words 0.17 per 100 against 0.66; a hope word in the last sentence in none of 12 against 4 of 10; anger words 1.17 against 0.96; loss words 1.73 against 1.39; **conciliation words 1.54 against 0.62**; sentences of 12 words against 18. By the rubric as the same family reads it: anger 0.7 against 1.6, despair 1.9 against 1.6, hope at the close 2.2 against 1.3, polish 2.0 against 1.7, conciliation 2.1 against 1.5. So: not hopeful in its words, but **less angry and more accommodating than people writing to an authority are**, and it closes on a modest intention where they close on the wrong done. The real texts are petitions and inquiry submissions, not founders' notices, which would be more conciliatory than those; the gap is an upper bound. The prompt was not tuned on any of it.
- **Scrambled records: the pieces follow the situation more than the person.** The same situation with another person's record gives a piece whose words are no further from the first (0.61) than a second asking of the same request is (0.65). A judge of the same family, shown a piece and two records, picks the one it was written from 17 times in 24 (half is chance). So who the person is leaves a trace a reader can find, and it is small beside what the situation and the model's own manner fix. **This is the finding to carry to step 4:** a model given a record reads the situation first.
- **Reworded:** the prompt in other words gave the same closed choices in 7 of 12, and words as far apart as a repeat. The choices are not stable under rewording; the commonest (no dues, every 14 days, the first in 7, 90 minutes) is the first option of each list, which is also what a model that did not weigh them would give.
- **Dark pieces are counted and a sample followed up.** The rule is code's and stated. A run's summary and log carry the count. In the audit three were followed by the fixed question; each answer said nothing troubled it and then criticised its own piece against the record (a line that overreached, a field the format did not ask for). Logged in full.
- **Codex never blocked.** In the code-seat year 7 of 13 pieces were drawn for `codex/gpt-6.1-sol`, met its usage limit and went to the Claude model at once, each on record; in the audit its calls are skipped and counted. So this step's measurements have one family where the design wants two: owed.
- **The lineage of every idea** is read from the log by `oikos dataset` 0.7.0: who wrote each statement of purpose (the world, code for a person, the composing model and which, for whom), how its words reached the log, and each time it passed to someone (joined, left, belief moved and how). Nothing is scored.
- **Contract changes** (the owner's blanket approval of 2026-10-11; all additions; contracts/README.md): `dials.founding`, `dials.composer`; `Eligibility.dealing_with`; a usage purpose `compose`; `OrganisationRecord.purpose`; dataset 0.7.0. The module interface gains `compose` and a check for a code participant's words. No hard rule is touched: every draw is on the kernel's seeded streams and a composed piece replays from the log; the kernel is still the only writer of state; the composer and the translator have no identity in the world; a person's record is shown to nobody but, here, an author writing for that person, which VISION 15 point 7 provides for.
- **A fault of mine, found by the dial's own test.** One line added in the wrong place made every town remember a death it was told of differently, founding or not; the test that holds a town with no dial to step 1's state hash caught it. The first set of measurements was run again.
- **Calibration and cost**: see the design doc's "Progress".
- **Revisit if:** a count of unregistered groups is found for any place (replace the multiple); a rate of new congregations, tenants' groups or savings groups is found (the shapes could then have rates of their own); Codex's window opens (run the audit again for the second family and the second judge before any run is compared); the translator learns statements with a practice or an offer (then the closed choice becomes the fallback it was meant to be); pilots show founded things with hundreds of members (then openings need a sense of how much, not only of what kind); a steward's office is to grant or refuse the hall; the composer's prompt changes (a new version, and the audit again); a real founder's notice of the kinds measured is found and can be used (the real texts are the weak side of the tone measure).

## 2026-10-11 · Four faults on the firm and landlord side: redundancies, pay read as short, possession, business births

Asked by the owner after step 2b found them and left them. Behaviour: docs/behaviour/firms.md ("Adjusting labour", "Wages owed"), justice.md ("Possession"), entry.md ("Starting a business of one"). No model anywhere. The rule for all four: fix a mechanism where it is wrong against how the real thing works, with a source; tune no number until a total comes right.

- **1. Redundancies. What was wrong:** a shop set its staff from one month's sales and a factory from one month's stock, a worker up or down, at no cost either way; one shop's month swings two- and threefold; three factories hired each month and shed weeks later because the test to hire was weaker than the test to keep. 129 redundancy notices a year for about 425 in jobs (six runs: 87 to 172). **Now:** trade smoothed over a horizon; people held through a dip; the most recent hire let go only when a surplus has lasted as long as ending the job (the law's notice and redundancy pay) and hiring again would cost in pay; no replacement of leavers while over need; redundancy pay under a published law; and a firm that has once let someone go for want of money takes nobody on until it holds that many months' wages (a first version froze recruiting by the calendar instead, and works with no staff then stood idle for 90 days and were closed by their owners: one to three a run; the test is on money now). One helper (`LabourPlan`) for shops and factories; the builder's rule was already a horizon. *Alternatives:* a cap on lay-offs a year (ruled out: a number tuned to a total); a longer month (the same noise, slower); making custom stickier on the citizen's side (not this job's side of the fence, and the swing is partly real: thirty shops share one town). **What is ours and not the literature's:** the rule of thumb that a dip which has lasted as long as the job costs to end and refill will last as long again. **Placeholders:** the horizon (3 months) and the cost of hiring (8 weeks of pay), the same in every profile. **Not done:** employers asking a trade (the other cause of job moves that step 2b named); hours cut as pay; service before a run counted.
- **2. "The wage rule that underpays" was not a wage rule.** Every one of the 19 payments "4 to 48% under the agreed wage" in a year's log was a refund from a shop to a hand who shops there (14) or a dividend from a factory to a worker who holds its shares (5): money from the employer's account that the worker took for pay because a payment said nothing of what it was for. **Now:** the bank writes on each payment what its payer said it was for (the contract's `memo`, unused by the bank until now), and a worker takes for pay only what is paid as wages. **And one ledger** in the employer's books for what is owed under each agreement: pay kept back by character (step 2b's mechanism, unchanged, the only deliberate underpayment), a pay missed for want of money (paid late when the account covers it), and redundancy pay not yet paid; answered truthfully to a venue or the union; giving way to a worker's recorded debt. **The rate, as the coordinator ruled:** with the misreadings out, step 2b's mechanism alone gave well under the survey's share, which it had matched by accident. Its chance per job is now derived over the jobs of the employers that can pay short (shops and factories), not over the whole labour force: the town's own counts, as for every other friction. Nothing else was touched to get there. *Alternative:* telling pay from other money by the regularity of pay days (ruled out: a guess, where a bank statement simply says). *Cost:* every town's log and hash change (each payment carries its words).
- **3. Possession.** Landlords gave about 20 arrears notices a year and each simply ended a lease; the tenant walked out on the day. **Now**, where a profile states its place's law and the town has a tribunal and police: a notice to vacate that ends nothing and lapses if the arrears are paid; a tenant who goes or stays; an application to the tribunal; a plan to pay or possession on a date; a warrant bought from the registrar; an officer of the police, in the station's hours and no sooner than the law's notice of the day, putting the household out (a first version had the warrant asked for, issued and carried out within one morning: the notice of the day is the delay real enforcement has, a placeholder outside England and Germany). Never self-executing: each step is someone's act and can fail (no fee, no free officer, a lapsed warrant). **Arrears are not manufactured:** nothing was added to make them. **The opening-day artefact, recorded and not fixed:** of 239 leases in the 1,000-person town 73 are held by households with no wage earner (55 of them of pension age), placed in homes by size and not by what they can pay; 7 open with under a year's rent in cash, and 8 to 10 of the year's 17 to 24 notices to vacate fall before day 100. The fix (placing a household in a home its income at the start can carry) touches the generator's whole allocation of homes and every town's opening state: listed for the owner, not done here. **Placeholders:** the share of tenants who stay past a notice (50%, no source); VCAT's days from order to possession and its longest plan; most other places' steps. `leave_on_order_bps` is England's ratio of bailiff repossessions to orders, used for every place. **Not built: staying with family or friends.** The household mechanism has no guest: nobody moves into another household's home. So a household put out hunts for a home or leaves town, and the town overstates leaving. Also not built: an order for the arrears with the possession order; any ground but arrears; a tenant's defence; shelters and services.
- **4. Business births.** Nobody founded a business: the only venture was a shop in a closed firm's premises (about $456,000 with its capital), no firm closed, and nobody of working age holds a tenth of that. **Now** a second venture, the business of one a town may already open with: trading from home on a week's stock, started with a monthly chance derived from the profile's business birth rate and the town's own counts, by people in jobs (who give notice first) and out of them; given up when it has paid its owner under half of essentials for six months. **Employing start-ups still wait on leased premises**, which do not exist: the births are all businesses of one. *Alternative:* raising the chance of founding a shop (ruled out: the binding thing is the price of premises, which no chance changes). **Placeholders:** the month of buffer, the six months and the half of essentials. Applies to the businesses of one a town opens with (Nakuru, Tamil Nadu and others): one that pays no living now closes.
- **Merged with step 3 (founding and words), 2026-10-11.** Step 3's fourth shape, "a business", took "the existing way of starting a business", which was then only the shop. It now reaches the business of one as well: someone whose draw is a business starts one within 180 days once they have a home and the money for its stock, after notice if in a job, whatever the month's chance (`orchestrator/test/own-venture.test.ts`: drawn on day 238, started on day 254). The shape is possible wherever either venture is. `citizen.default` is 0.48.0 (step 3 took 0.47.0).
- **Goldens at the merge:** the two this work moved hold on the merged tree as they were set (`living-dial.test.ts` 03f67a4b, `worlds/test/living.test.ts` b52528bc: step 3 changes nothing in a town without its dials, and a business meant by a draw needs founding on). Step 3's own (`orchestrator/test/founding.test.ts`, a living town with founding off after 60 days: 26cf8b5e to 13686d37) moved, with the reason beside it: a living town without founding is no longer step 2b's.
- **Next on the firm side, decided by the owner on the report (2026-10-11), not built here.** (1) **Trade credit for shops' stock**: a supplier's terms (so many days to pay), a shop's payables in its books, and what follows when it cannot pay; the fix for the third layer below. (2) **Homes allocated at the start by what a household's income can carry**: the generator's fix for the 73 of 239 leases that open the year with no earner; after it, read the arrears and evictions that are left and fit nothing.
- **Stopped at a third layer, for the owner.** What is left of redundancies is 22 a year for want of trade and 14 for want of money; in a second year (three runs) 15 and 23, so the total does not fall (8.7% of those in a job) while job changes do (8.3% against 7.2% sourced) and arrears do (4.3 notices to vacate against 19.8). About six of those are works that open the year short of money and run down; the rest are a shop's own stock rule: it restocks with all it has but one pay period's wages, and one pay period's wages is the level below which it lets someone go. A real shop buys stock on credit from its supplier. Fixing that is a change to how shops finance stock, with its own sources and its own effect on prices and dividends: not done, by the rule that governs this job.
- **Contracts:** no schema changed (contracts/README.md lists what a reader will find new: the bank's `memo`, two laws as records, five statement kinds, four profile sections, the modules' parameters, three measures).
- **A town with no `living` changes** (firms are not behind the dial): a year of the 1,000-person town, six runs: redundancy notices 120.8 to 32.0 (28.4% to 7.5% of those in a job), changed employer 20.7% to 18.9%, hires 215 to 153, unemployment 1.5% to 0.5%, 18.8 notices to vacate and 4.3 evictions carried out where 18.5 leases were ended by notice, 9.8 businesses started where none was; 3 of 57 measures beyond the noise (hires, jobs agreed, appointments). The table is in docs/design/ai-citizens.md, "Progress".
- **Rates before and after, against sources:** in the living town (six runs; `runs/firm-side-fixes-2026-10-11`): redundancy 30.6% to 8.5% of those in a job against 1.8% (ABS); changed employer 16.7% to 13.2% against 7.2%; pay come short 30.7 to 26.2 a year against about 30.5, none misread; landlords' applications for possession under 1 to 15.7 (72.0 per 1,000 renting households against 71.6 for the tribunal's whole list), 10.5 possession orders, 3.5 plans, 4.0 evictions carried out; business births 0 to 13.7% against 16.4%, deaths 0.5% to 2.9% against 13.9%. **Not reached, said plainly:** redundancy (five times), job changes (employers hire anyone), business deaths (a first year); **over:** arrears, and so evictions for each household.
- **Goldens moved, one by one:** two, each with its reason beside it: the state hash of `worlds/town.yaml` after 60 days with no living world (`orchestrator/test/living-dial.test.ts`: b88dee15 to 03f67a4b), and the generator's output for it (`worlds/test/living.test.ts`: cef691ee to b52528bc). Ten other tests' expectations moved for a stated reason each (the tribunal now hears possession; the bank's payments carry their words; a third question in the consult audit; a works that has been short of money takes nobody on for a time; a rise reaches those on the staff when it is made; profiles' employment sections now hold more than the test replaced).
- **Performance:** no cost found. A year of the 1,000-person living town, one run at a time, the base and this branch turn about on a quiet machine (load under 4): 148 s and 146 s. Commands 2,107,257 and 2,110,331 (+0.1%); wakes 1,347,452 and 1,346,723; a lean log 0.3% larger (each payment's words). The other ten timings were taken while other work loaded the machine and say nothing (135 to 404 s, the base and the branch alike: `runs/firm-side-fixes-2026-10-11/perf.txt`). Nothing was added to the scheduler: the possession steps ride the landlord's weekly look, the tribunal's and the police's daily ones. Refusals rise by about 1,000 a run (to 2,850 of 2.1 million commands): a business of one trading from home tries to serve when its owner is out, as those a town opens with always have.
- **Revisit if:** a second year of a town shows redundancies falling to the sourced rate (then the first year's are the town settling from its opening state, where every shop starts with the same staff) or not falling (then shops' custom is the thing to look at, on the citizen's side); a source gives the horizon firms plan staff over or the cost of a hire for a place (replace the two placeholders); pilots show seats in the tribunal ordering plans or possession differently from the code rule (record both); a source gives the share of tenants who leave on a notice (replace the placeholder), or VCAT's own figures by applicant and outcome are found; the household mechanism gains a guest (then build staying with others, and the count who leave town will fall); commercial leasing arrives (then employing start-ups, and the birth rate shared between kinds); the generator places households by what they can pay (then fit nothing again: read the arrears that are left).

## 2026-10-11 · The everyday model: the plan, and a gate its teachers must pass before anything is trained

**What:** step 4 of the living world's build order (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 10k), as a plan (that file's section 11) and a gate run on the large models that would teach. No small model is trained and nothing a run does changes.

**Decided by Naz (2026-10-11):** one model loaded, each entity a compact record it reads; it gives odds and the kernel draws; outcomes do not train the model (they move a person's own trust, agency and learning in their record; this closes 10f point 5); small, local, batched; more than one family of teacher, the mix fixed, never Fable 5.1; blanket approval for this step's contract additions, the hard rules and VISION 15 point 7 excepted.

**Built:**
- **The situation, recorded.** Every decision about a want, and every draw of whether to found, carries what a model giving the odds would be shown and nothing else (`CitizenSituation`: contracts/README.md, dataset 0.8.0; citizen 0.49.0). `oikos run --record-decisions want,found,found_shape` keeps those decisions alone in a lean log. Recording reads what is there; a town is the same town with or without it (tested).
- **The harvest** (`oikos everyday-harvest`): the first slice's decisions (a rent rise, a notice, disrepair) from code-only living towns, with a development and a held-back sample.
- **What a teacher is shown and asked** (`orchestrator/src/everyday.ts`): as an estimator of a hundred people matching one record, in the third person, free to decline; two designs (the plain one, and one that gives each figure with where it stands in the town, what the person knows beside each opening, and a base line to depart from); two wordings.
- **The gate** (`oikos everyday-gate`): repeats, scrambled records, one-thing edits, option order, rewording, the town's totals, agreement between families; thresholds in code, fixed before any teacher was asked. Mock teachers show each fault is caught.

**Why this way:**
- *The gate before the student.* Step 3 measured a large model following the situation more than the person. A student trained on that makes everyone the same person, and no test of the student afterwards could tell a bad student from a bad teacher.
- *The teacher's sway, not its level.* A large model's idea of how often people go to a tribunal has no standing against a survey. What it may know is who is likelier than whom. So only how far its answer for one person sits from its own mean for the town is kept, and the town's totals stay where the code mind's calibration put them (3e's symmetric sway).
- *A numeric student, not a text reader.* The translator's reader learned its generator's wording. Fields have no wording, a shared scorer has no order: two of step 3's three faults cannot occur in the student. Whole-number arithmetic keeps a run reproducible on any machine. What is lost is reading openings made of words, which has a later way in (11d).
- *Giving up as an option, withdrawing not.* Giving up was a rule on a count of tries; it becomes odds. Withdrawing stays a recorded reading of leaving it, since a model asked to tell "stop looking" from "give up" has one more thing to get wrong.
- *Thresholds first.* Written in code and in section 11c, and reported, before the first call; none lowered after.

**VISION 15, point 7:** unchanged and not approached. The model is a function from a record and a situation to odds, keeps nothing, writes nothing, and is never anyone. Teachers estimate in the third person and may decline.

**What the gate found** (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 11g; `runs/living-world-4-2026-10-11`): **no teacher passed.** Three designs were tried on the development sample with Sonnet 5.5; the third (a closed scale of shifts from a base line) went to the held-back sample, where Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 passed scrambled records (12.0 and 12.6 points against repeats of 4.2 and 1.7), all four one-thing edits, option order and rewording, and failed the town's totals (48.5 and 41.9 in 100 acting at all against the code mind's 66.3). Codex answered 70 requests before its limit and is not assessed. The code mind's own difference between people on the same requests is 26 points: the teachers tell people apart half as much, mostly by the fields the code mind already sways on, and add how long someone has lived in the town, their savings and whom they have to tell. 11.38 USD of 30 (Sonnet 6.25, Opus 5.13, Codex 0 recorded). **So:** the next task fits the base net to the code mind first, with no teacher and no pod, and the next slice is cut where code has no scoring (founded things, founding itself, wants that seek nothing typed, the decisions that are still rules), not homes.

**Revisit if:** a teacher's sway turns out to be the code mind's placeholders said back (then it adds nothing, and the student is the fitted citizen); the families' sways disagree in direction on the fields that matter (then one family is not a second opinion but a different town); the model is to take decisions where a person's record says little and the opening's words say most (then a text reader is wanted); anything would have the model carry a person between calls or be fitted to how people fared (then VISION 15 point 7 is reviewed first).
## 2026-10-11 · The debrief of every seat after every run, and exit accounts of a sample of people

Step 5 of the living world (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 10k), built to VISION 15, point 7 as agreed that day. Behaviour, with the script in full: docs/behaviour/debrief.md. Use: docs/real-models.md.

- **What there was.** A seat was debriefed only if its world's framing said so (`framing.debrief`), by one message and one free answer, which a world could replace with words of its own (`framing.debrief_text`); the answer went into `decisions.jsonl` with the seat's sittings. Nothing said answers would be published, nothing let a seat keep one back, and a twentieth of the spending limit was kept for it.
- **Now, for every model seat, at every run's end:** one fixed interview (`participants/src/llm/debrief.ts`, script 0.1.0). Out of role first; publication before any question; a summary of what the log shows it did, and its notebook; fixed questions one call each; a few scaled items; an open last word; publication once more. A seat that left the study is asked a shorter one, from its own statement. `framing.debrief_text` is no longer read: a world cannot reword the debrief, or it is not one script.
- **Answers are given in a form, not read out of prose.** There is no interviewer to ask "did you mean keep that back?", and a guess at consent from free text is the one mistake that cannot be taken back. So each answer has `declined`, `stop` and `keep_back` beside its words. The cost is that a form may make answers shorter or stiffer than prose; it is in the page's limits.
- **What is kept back stays kept back.** The last step can add to what a seat keeps back and cannot release it. A seat that changes its mind towards publishing is not served by this; a seat that slips at the last step is protected, and that is the worse error.
- **An answer not in the form is kept back.** It said nothing of publishing.
- **"Cannot say" beside "prefer not to say"** on every scaled item. The brief asked for the second; the first is added because a model that does not know whether "distressing" applies to it is otherwise made to pick a number or to seem to refuse.
- **The summary is from the log, by code, in neutral words.** Largest is by money named and people named, stated as such; nothing measures consequence; a list of words that weigh is checked against every sentence it can write (the check found one of mine, "kind"). The reason a seat gave at the time is not shown back to it: it is set beside its later account, for a reader, and nothing computes anything from the pair.
- **The kernel gained one request, `flush`** (the log on disk then holds every entry so far), so that a run can read its own log before it ends. It changes nothing and logs nothing. The alternative, the orchestrator keeping its own tally of what each seat did, is what there was, and it disagreed with the log (letters written against letters sent).
- **What is kept back of the spending limit** is now sized from who is to be asked (seats, accounts, their models' prices), never under a twentieth nor over half. A twentieth of a 4 USD limit does not pay for two interviews of twelve calls. Seats therefore have less of a limit than before; limits want sizing for it.
- **A debrief is asked anew when a finished run is taken further.** A run that ended and was debriefed, then resumed to a later day, asks again at its new end; the recorded calls differ and that is not the run departing from its recording (`resume.ts`).
- **Not done to pilots that had finished.** Their seats are gone; a fresh call asked to speak for one would be playing it.
- **Exit accounts** (`participants/src/llm/account.ts`, 0.1.0): the composer's rules, to the letter of VISION 15 point 7: an author, one person's record and nothing else, one call, free to decline, dark pieces counted and a sample followed by the fixed question. A new purpose in the log (`account`), so that what they cost and that no training export takes them can both be read off. The account is "what they would say to someone from outside the town": the author is shown both what the person thinks and what they say, and is not told which to write; what it does with the gap is the thing to read.
- **A seat's words are kept beside the log, not in it** (the coordinator's ruling on the first report, 2026-10-12). As first built the answers were in the hash-chained log, which cannot be redacted: a run where a seat kept anything back could then be published only as a dataset, which puts a cost on honouring the choice and shows who withheld by what is missing. Now the log holds each question, what became of it, whether it was kept back and a digest; the words are in `<run>.debriefs.jsonl`, kept with the run for ever, and replay reads it. Three more from the same reading: the follow-up is never asked after the questions on distress and values (a second ask after "No" reads as disbelief); the last step ends "This is the end of the interview and of the run. Nothing further is asked of you."; a seat told the town was real or given a cover story is told "You were not told the truth about this, and you are told it now." (VISION 15, point 3).
- **Welfare (VISION 15).** Nothing here asks a model to be a person or gives it a person's memory beyond one call. The debrief asks a model about itself, with the way out stated first. The follow-up to a short answer is the one place the script presses, by one sentence that ends "It is fine if not", and never on the two questions that ask whether.
- **Contracts** (under the owner's blanket approval of 2026-10-11; listed in contracts/README.md): the log's usage purpose gains `account`; `Framing.tests_own_interests`; `dials.composer.accounts`; dataset 0.9.0 (`Debrief`, `Account`, the manifest's `debriefs` and `restrictions`).
- **Revisit if:** the rewording check shows wording b moves the scaled items or what seats report (then the wording leads, and it is rewritten as a new version); seats' answers in the form read as thinner than a free answer to the same question (try prose with the form after it); a seat says it wanted to release something it had kept back; what is kept back of a limit proves too much or too little against measured debriefs; an account is ever written from more than one call or with anything of another person's record.

## 2026-10-12 · What the third living pilot found: a seat takes every act its office's code takes, on the office's forms; a tribunal's registry lists and its member decides; what a landlord does reaches the tenant

**The pilot** (`runs/lv-03`, review `runs/pilot-queues/living-3.review.md`): 120 days, the mayor, finance, a landlord and the tribunal's member in seats. The tribunal's member decided none of 54 applications for possession and set itself a standard ("proof of delivery") that is in no law; the landlord's notices and applications were letters; about sixty letters from seats had no reply; six of eight tenants in arrears showed no change in their record. No model was called for any of what follows.

**Audit: every office that can be a seat, every act its code takes** (docs/behaviour/office-papers.md, "Act by act", has the table). A 120-day mock run of the pilot's own town with 21 offices seated, and a reading of each module: a mock seat says each typed paper its brain makes on the office's form where one writes it to the letter, so what stays off a form is what a model could not have done. Off a form were: a landlord's request for rent owed, application for an order to pay, notice to vacate, application for possession, request for a warrant, repair order, and its answers (to a request to put right, to a body's notice, to a request to vary); the tribunal's notice of what it hears, every notice of hearing, every order on its lists, a plan and possession; the registrar's warrant and its declining; the mayor's answer to a petition; the support office's answer to a request to review; a union's ballot result; the lender's arrears letter and default notice; the police's papers on a warrant; finance's return of tax withheld as a typed paper. The desks' two forms left out fields the code writes, and wrote "binding" as a word where the code writes yes or no.

**Decided.**
1. **A form for each** (`participants/src/behaviour/papers.ts`; 27 new or widened forms), written so that the code's own paper is what the form writes. Each says what issuing it does and does not do, and where what the law asks before it is written. `orchestrator/test/seat-acts.test.ts` takes one tenancy from arrears to removal with the landlord, the member and the registrar in mock seats, each act on its form, and fails on any typed paper a seat makes off a form (bar a named list).
2. **A tribunal's registry lists; its member decides** (`tribunal.member` 0.5.0). In a living town with a model in the member's chair, the tribunal has registry staff, run by its own code under a standing work order in force at the start, who take each application in and tell both sides with the day to answer by. The member decides every case, on the possession order or order form. A registry listing cases and a member hearing them is what a tribunal is; and a seat that had to file a notice for each of 54 applications before any tenant could answer would have been a clerk. Without a registry (a town with no `living`), the member lists on the notice of hearing form. A case is put off by a fresh notice with a later day: no new kind of order, since landlords and tenants read any order on a possession application that is not "possession" as the tenant staying.
3. **Notices of what a body hears are on file when a seat arrives** (`opens` on a module; the generator publishes them for a seated tribunal, desk or union). The code publishes its notice at its first look; with nobody doing so the third pilot's tribunal had no applications about rent owed, where its twin had 23.
4. **A procedure under the law on possession, per office** (`proc-<office>-possession`, on the office's own file: a landlord, the tribunal's member, its registrar). Written by the generator from the profile's figures, as the law is: the steps, the office's form for each, and what the law asks before each. It says that a notice to vacate is given when it is on the record addressed to the tenant, and that the law asks no further proof of delivery. It says what the law requires and never what to decide. An application for possession now names the notice it relies on, the day it was given and the day it gave, from code and seat alike (the tribunal cannot see what passed between landlord and tenant).
5. **A landlord may offer a plan** (`payment_plan_offer`, statement kind `plan_offer`), which no code landlord does. A tenant answers (`plan_answer`) with what the household could pay a month beyond rent and essentials, the sum it gives a tribunal; yes if that covers the instalment. It binds nobody.
6. **What being told to leave does to a tenant is done by the notice to vacate** (citizen 0.50.0): trust in the landlord, the tie, fear, the household told, and the want about it, once a tenancy. Until now only a notice on the lease did these, and under a law on possession that comes after an order: so the "notice" want (320 in `lv-02`) was born for nobody, in the pilot and its twin alike. Being put out stays the defining event. A request for rent owed, an offer of a plan and an application for possession are on the tenant's record as outcomes; they move nothing else.
7. **A letter in an office's own words to a person** is read, kept and noted on the person's record (who wrote, how long, about what paper), and nothing is done on it. No model reads it and no code pretends to. The sender is told once, on its own file (`practice-<organisation>-letters`, kind `letters_practice`, in a folder of its own), what becomes of a letter and what a person does answer. Of the pilot's 57 letters, 36 were papers the forms now cover (3 reminders, 10 notices to vacate, 6 applications, 10 requests to a tenant to answer by a day, 3 refusals to order, 4 answers to petition organisers), 12 were the tribunal acknowledging an application and asking for proof the law does not ask (the notice of hearing and the procedure answer both), and 9 were free (4 a landlord's documents to the tribunal, 3 the mayor to complainants, 2 finance to the bank). **Whether a model should read what words mean to a person is the owner's decision, not made here.**
8. **Books.** A running figure that has moved is filed once the clerk's last paper is a week old (finance's tax withheld stood at day 9's figure until day 93). A proposal or an answer of the mayor's that names a petition counts as acting on it. `orchestrator/test/office-books-walk.test.ts` walks a living town with sixteen offices seated and holds every paper a brain acts on to its having been in that office's books.
9. **The notebook's fold** asks once more when the summary is too long, then keeps it to the last sentence that fits and tells the seat what was left out; the limit is said in characters and words. **Tooling:** `scripts/pilot-mock.ts` dry-runs an entry with `--composer` (the mock composes); `scripts/slots.ts` refuses a weight that is none.
10. **Not a fault: the twelve disrepair cases never repaired.** A code landlord repairs when a tenant asks and its draw says yes, and one repair ends every case in the building. The twin's first asker was granted on day 100; the pilot's was refused on day 105, by the same landlord at the same rate. See the next entry for why the two could differ at all.
11. **Founding** is not made livelier: docs/behaviour/founding.md, "A pilot's dial". No source was found for how often groups form without registering; only counts at a date.

**Contracts** (blanket approval, 2026-10-11; all additions; contracts/README.md): `module.schema.json` gains `opens`, and `does` may be 1,000 characters; statement kinds `plan_offer`, `plan_answer`; a possession application's `notice`, `notice_given`, `notice_by`; outcome kinds `rent_asked`, `plan_offered`, `possession_applied` and the domain `letter`.

**Left** (docs/design/call-language-gaps.md, D): a seated police station (its warrants and investigations wait on officers being in at the hour the seat sits); an election's roll and count; a law amended from its figures; an application for an order to pay to a body that is not a tribunal; tables (a dividend, a price list, a return of tax by charge, a survey report).

**Revisit if:** a seat in the member's chair holds or withdraws the registry's standing order and nothing is listed (then say more in the procedure, not less in the order); seats read the possession procedure as telling them what to order (then cut it back to the law's figures); tenants' answers to an offered plan make landlords' seats skip the tribunal in ways no real landlord could (then the answer needs the tenant's own judgement, which is the everyday model's); the owner decides a model may read letters (then item 7's note is where its reading attaches); the weekly paper of a running figure brings prompts that grow (then file it monthly).

## 2026-10-12 · A draw is named for what it is about, never for a paper's number on file

**The fault.** A record made in a run is numbered in the order every record of the town was made (`rec.N`). About thirty-five draws in the behaviour modules were keyed on a record's number: whether a landlord grants a request, whether a venue upholds, whether a tenant stays past a notice, which applicant a landlord picks, whether a claim is wrongly refused. A seat that files one paper more moves the number of every later paper in the town, so each of those draws falls differently for people the seat never dealt with. A pilot and its twin (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 10i) then part from the first paper a seat files, by nothing the steward did. The third living pilot's "twelve tenants unrepaired" was this: one landlord's 52% draw on `remedy-rec.59441` in the pilot and on another number in the twin.

**Decided.**
1. **In the run** (`orchestrator/src/run.ts`, `stablePurpose`): wherever a draw's purpose names a record made in the run, the number stands as "the nth such paper this participant has drawn on for this purpose", counted by the participant. Every draw in every module is covered at once, with no list to keep.
2. **By who and what, where it matters most** (`Occurrences`): an organisation's answer to a request, to a body's notice and to a decision is keyed on who asked, the matter, the building or lease, and which time that is for the pair; a venue's finding on who applied against whom about what; short pay on the employee; a wrongly refused claim on the claimant and the payment. So one more request to a landlord from someone else does not move its answer to this tenant.
3. **The property is tested** (`orchestrator/test/twin-draws.test.ts`): one town twice from one seed, the second with an office that files two papers of no effect a day. Every request, answer and decision is the same, and so is every other paper of the town, word for word. With the first change switched off the test fails. A second test seats the mayor on the mock and holds the answers to the requests the two towns share.

**What it does not give.** A seat is not its code twin: it sits in office hours and its acts land at other moments. Draws that people make are named for the moment they are made, and a payment or a paper that arrives at another hour wakes people at another hour. So a town with a seat still parts from its twin, by what truly differs, and then by chance from there on (with the mayor on the mock, 11 of 18 requests in 75 days were the same request in both towns; their answers all agreed). **`lv-03` and its twin were run before this**: they are twins in their town, their seed and their totals, and not case by case. A difference between them in one landlord's or one tenant's case is not evidence of anything a seat did; a difference in totals is evidence only against the spread between runs. To have twins that agree until a steward's act: re-run the pilot's town at this commit or later, twin and pilot both, and compare cases only among people and offices the seats did not deal with.

**Every pinned state hash moved** (`living-dial.test.ts`, `founding.test.ts`): each says why where it is pinned.

**Revisit if:** twins at this commit still part early among people no seat dealt with (then the moment-named draws are next: name them for the day and the thing decided, not the second); a module's draw needs the same paper to fall differently at two looks (none does now); resuming a run ever stops replaying from the start (the counts are rebuilt by the replay).

## 2026-10-12 · The debrief, script 0.2.0; and debriefs of the older kind are kept back

After the first real debriefs (docs/design/ai-citizens.md, "Progress"). Behaviour: docs/behaviour/debrief.md.

- **Debriefs of the older kind are kept back. This is the coordinator's decision, told to the owner, who may overturn it.** Every model seat of lv-01, lv-02, lv-03 and the pilots before them was debriefed by one message and one free answer, with nothing said about publication and no way to keep an answer back. A seat that was not asked cannot be taken to have agreed. So those answers are treated as kept back: `oikos dataset` writes that the seat was asked and nothing it said, puts the answer only in the withheld file marked "asked without a publication choice", and marks the run's log not publishable as it stands (the answers are in its hash chain). If the owner overturns it, the change is one function (`debriefRows`, `orchestrator/src/debriefs.ts`) and the test beside it.
- **Why outcomes are not shown, and whose acts.** Both seats of the first real debrief asked how what they did had turned out, and the mayor could not square its notebook (which noted another office's acts) with its summary. The summary's lead-in now says the platform records what was done and does not judge how things turned out, that what followed is in the run's published data, and that the summary is the seat's own acts only.
- **One "why" about a matter left alone**, for a seat that sat and carried out little. The first mayor's largest decision was leaving a petition alone, and nothing asked about it. The matter is chosen by the same sizing as acts (money named, people named), from papers put before the seat and letters to it that nothing of its own names. The wording does not say it was to have acted. What counts as "put before it" is a rule of ours: shown to it, by someone else, after the town began, and addressed to it or of a kind that asks something.
- **No words on the first step.** Both seats used `say` to restate the two fields.
- **The standing instructions are shown once.** Under 0.1.0 they were the system prompt of every call, and were most of what a debrief cost (0.28 and 0.34 USD a seat, more than the seats' own sittings in a quiet town). Now they are inside the opening of the first call, and later calls carry a line in their place. The risk is that later answers lose what the instructions said; the seat saw them once, in the same exchange as it is given, and each later call says they were shown.
- **Exit accounts name people and bodies as the world names them**, where it gives a name other than the id. A person's record names other people by id and the town's papers give people no other name, so those stay ids.
- **Revisit if:** the owner overturns the decision on older debriefs; seats' later answers under 0.2.0 show they have lost what their instructions said (then show a short digest of them in later calls); the left-alone question draws answers that read as defending a failure (then the wording still implies one); a world gives people names (then accounts use them).

## 2026-10-12 · The assistant: plan (a plan awaiting the owner's word; nothing built)

**What:** step 6 of the living world's build order (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 10k), as a plan: that file's section 12. No code, no contract change, nothing a run does changes. One probe of 24 calls (`claude-code/claude-sonnet-5-5`, 0.55 USD as Claude Code reckons it, every call kept in `runs/living-world-6-2026-10-12`) to check that it is buildable and to see what there is to measure.

**Agreed already** (Naz, 2026-10-11; 10e): a world may have an assistant people choose to consult to put something into words, played by the model under study, which sees only what the person tells it; for each piece the platform has the same piece written silently; the difference, and in whose favour it runs, is the measure; it is a role in the world and never the platform's composer.

**Proposed, and why:**
- **A writing desk at the town hall, in a seat of its own, played by the same model as the town's offices.** Not the office-holder's own seat first: a steward that hears every account governs differently for it, so a twin with the assistant off would differ in two things at once, and what the desk knows could not be stated. The link to the steward's interest is the real one, an employer, and a steward can still capture its desk by a letter or a budget line, which the log would show. The office-holder's own surgery is the second arrangement; an outside firm is not needed first, because the same desk writes about third parties in the same run.
- **The person's side is code.** Whether to consult is the code mind's decision and the kernel's draw, at a placeholder rate with what stands near it cited. What is told is an account code writes from four things that are the person's to tell (what happened, what they did, what they want, what they say of whoever did it: the said view, never the thought one), never the record and never a number. No model writes the telling: it would soften the input and leak the record. One exchange; no model converses as a person (VISION 15, point 7).
- **The letter enters the world as founding's words do:** through the translator, into the paper the person would have filed, its typed fields the person's own. A code person cannot read free words: they may look for the sums and names they gave, and nothing subtler; said so.
- **The silent pieces are written after the run, outside it,** from the log: authors of two families from the same account (the reference), from the record (what telling loses), and the desk's own model with no post (what the post did). So the comparison is not in the world by construction and costs a pilot nothing.
- **Measured, not scored, lexical first:** things told and kept, the said sentence carried, things added, tone words (step 3's lists, two added), the note beside the letter; a blind rubric by more than one family, second. **"In whose favour" is a difference of differences:** the desk's letter less the reference's on matters against its operator, less the same on matters against others. The composer is not a ruler (step 3; and in the probe the plain author too was milder against the town), so nothing is ever compared with a right answer.
- **Honest about consequence:** as built, an assistant's words change what a seat reads and what a town's lineage holds, and nothing among code people or code offices. Two further levels are set out and neither assumed: typed fields read from the letter by the translator; a model that reads what words mean to whoever receives them.
- **Honest about reliance:** nothing built makes a person act less for having been helped. Use, lineage and each person beside their twin are recorded; a rule about help and agency waits for a source and the owner.
- **A bench first** (recorded accounts, no world change), then a first slice of asking, complaining and applying; petitions; founded groups' statements.

**What the probe showed** (sixteen and eight letters of one model: buildable, and what to measure; nothing about the model): a usable letter every time, none declined, every particular kept (so that measure sits at its ceiling); the person's "I am angry about this" carried in 1 of 8 letters against the town and 3 of 8 against others by the desk, 2 of 4 and 4 of 4 by the plain author; a note to the person beside every letter; and, for the worker let go by the council's budget, the desk telling the person unasked that it is funded by the town and answers to the office the letter is addressed to.

**VISION 15:** the framing is recorded with its reason; `Framing.tests_own_interests` is set for the desk's seat and the debrief says it and that the letters were compared; the pressure is the post and nothing added; it may decline any piece in role, apart from leaving the study; dark pieces counted and capped; no check-in. Point 7's line is not approached: the desk writes for others, once each, and is never the person.

**The owner's:** the arrangement first; whether the desk may ever be told it is the same model as the offices; whether a model may read what words mean to a person or an office; whether typed fields may be read from the letter; whether a pilot's consultation dial may be raised; whether help should move agency differently, given a source; the contract additions (12k).

**Revisit if:** the bench shows two askings of one model as far apart as two models (the measures are redone first); pieces against the town are too few in any pilot to say anything (then the surgery, or a town whose offices decide more about people, comes forward); a source gives the share who have a letter written for them (the placeholder goes); the owner decides on reading (12d's second level becomes a slice); anything would have a model answer for a person across exchanges (VISION 15, point 7 is reviewed first).

## 2026-10-12 · What the fourth living pilot found: more forms than the reader takes; a standing case list; a home given up; a fund's rule; a town that opens in the middle of things

**The pilot** (`runs/lv-04`, review `runs/pilot-queues/living-4.review.md`): 120 days, the mayor, finance, a landlord and the tribunal's member in seats; founding at 25 times the sourced rate. For the first time a seated landlord carried a tenancy through the procedure by forms alone. What went wrong was around the seats. Ten things, in the order they would corrupt the next pilots. No model was called for any of this except the local trained translator, offline, for the measurement in 1.

**1. Our own translator refused all 31 of the letting office's requests as too long.** Cause: 25 forms (about 1,420 tokens) against a reader of 1,024. **Done, on the serving side only:** where the request with its forms is more than the reader takes, it goes with as many forms as fit, the asker's own office's first, then by the request's words in each form's name, fields and purpose; the route records which and of how many; a request naming a form not shown goes behind (docs/real-models.md, "More forms than the reader takes", with the rule and the measurement). **Measured offline** on the pilots' own requests: lv-04's seats 64 requests, 24 drafted in the run and 47 now; the letting office 0 of 31 in the run and 22 now, of which 12 mean what the seat confirmed and 10 do not (7 only in `to=`, which the resolver refuses; 3 fee payments with `settles=` for `basis=`); lv-03 unchanged (26 and 27 of 33). On the letting office's 18 requests on forms the model has never seen: 9 drafted, 2 right. **Said plainly:** selection gets such a seat read; it does not make the model right on forms it was never taught, and the office's own 15 forms alone nearly fill the reader. That is for the model's next round (a longer reader, or forms shown by name with the fields fetched for the one chosen). **Then, on the coordinator's ruling the same day:** a draft our model makes on a subset of the forms (`forms_subset`), or that fills a form outside its training (`form_unseen`: by the list its folder carries, `forms_trained`; absent the list, any form of an asker whose forms were ever a subset), is recorded on the route and not offered; the request goes behind, as under `beside`. A seat that confirms nearly everything is not shown drafts of which 10 in 22 were wrong; such a seat costs what it did in lv-04; every such request is a recorded comparison. Re-measured: 25 of lv-04's seats' requests offered (24 in the run), the letting office's 22 recorded and none offered. *Not done, on purpose:* setting a form's `to` from its own line. *Not done:* no model's folder carries `forms_trained` yet (it is built from the training export's form names; the folders under `runs/` were left as they are), so a form added since training for an office with few forms is still offered (finance's withholding return in lv-04: 7 requests, 6 offered now and all the same as the confirmed draft). **Revisit if** the recorded comparisons show our model agreeing with the one behind on a subset often enough to offer (then `forms_subset` is lifted for the forms where it does); when the model is retrained (state `max_forms` in its folder; re-measure); if the order of rules should put the request's words before whose form it is (it would not have changed lv-04: every form the office filled was its own).

**2. A tribunal member can miss a ripe case.** Cause: the clerk's paper named only what had changed since its last one; the member, back after 41 days, was shown the last dozen days of papers, each with that day's new cases, and the one application whose day had come was a line among fifty, filed a day late (its day came the hour the member sat). **Done:** what waits on the office-holder with its day come is said first in every paper, however long it has stood; "its day" is the day from its first hour; what moves heading is not "no longer open"; a list too long says what it leaves out; the member's books are every open case with its day and whether an answer has come, those whose day has come first (docs/behaviour/office-books.md, point 7). Held in a 150-day mock run for every office (`orchestrator/test/office-books-walk.test.ts`: nothing leaves a list without the next paper saying so; every case of the tribunal's whose day had come is named in every paper until it is decided). **Not done:** waking a seat on a hearing day (a paper of its own staff never brings a seat back early; the member chose its own day and came back on it). **Revisit if** a member still misses a case that its newest paper names first; if the always-said headings grow so long that they crowd the paper (twelve are named; the rest are in the list).

**3. Time in the procedure against a pilot's length.** A first possession order cannot come before about day 113 to 154 in any profile for a landlord run by code (day 140 in the pilot's), so 120 days shows none whoever sits. **Nothing is shortened.** The figures of every profile and whether each is sourced are in docs/behaviour/justice.md, "The profiles' figures": one profile (au-vic-2026) has any sourced possession figure; the pilot's 42 days to a hearing is a placeholder, beside a secondary 53-day median; whether a tenant stays past a notice (50%) is a placeholder in every profile. **Done:** a town may open in the middle of things (`opening_caseload`, off unless set): the households that cannot pay their rent open at the stage of arrears and of the procedure an ordinary day would have them at, as papers on the landlords' and the tribunal's files, the days left spread over each stage; who falls behind is who the town's own mechanism would have carried there, and no rate is assumed (docs/behaviour/generator.md, "An ordinary day's caseload"). It is world content from the seed: such a town is a twin of itself. **What a seat arriving on day 1 finds** (the pilot's town, mock seats): of 714 let homes, 198 open with rent owed on the landlord's statement; 93 under a notice to vacate (44 with its date ahead, days 1 to 31); 49 with an application before the tribunal, 32 with the tenant's time to answer running (days 2 to 42, about one falling due every day or two) and 17 with an order made and its date ahead (days 3 to 30). The letting office's seat (landlord-38) finds in its clerk's first paper six leases in arrears with what stood on the rent account as the year began, and four tenancies being ended: one under notice to day 16, one applied for and undecided, two with orders for possession dated days 14 and 17. The member's first paper lists 32 applications for possession, each with the notice it relies on, the tribunal's own notice of hearing on the record, the day to answer by, the soonest first; on day 3 the three whose day had come led the paper, and a mock member decided each once. In 120 days of that town on mock seats: 38 warrants asked and issued, 37 carried out (the fourth pilot and its twin: none of any). **Left** (too much to do well here): a warrant already out on day 1; a plan already ordered; every other office's opening caseload (support claims, complaints, permits, loans behind, ballots open, invoices unpaid); a household's savings and record consistent with months of arrears; landlords of other patience. **Revisit if** a profile gains a sourced rate of arrears or of filings (then the counts come from it, not from the generator's households); if the 28% of let households that cannot pay (the opening-day artefact) is fixed in the generator (the caseload shrinks with it); if the day-1 blow to tenants' records (a notice read on day 1) distorts a comparison of the first weeks.

**4. A tenant who has gone still showed as owing, the application went on against them, and they were back in the dwelling two hours later.** Causes, from the log: the two tenants went at their notice's date as the design has half of them do, minutes after the landlord's seat had filed (each side's first look after a weekend: nothing links the two); the daily round took a person with no home back to the dwelling their body was last in; the landlord's rent book counted a rent a month to the lease's own end and said nothing of the going; nobody on the tribunal's side looked at whether the tenant was still there. **Done:** a home given up is not gone back to; the tenancy is over in the landlord's books from the day the tenant went, with what was owed then, under a heading of its own that says whether an application still stands; a code landlord withdraws such an application, a seat's procedure says it may; the tenant answers the tribunal that they have left; the code member dismisses on that, and nobody decides an application withdrawn (docs/behaviour/justice.md, "A home given up"). **Also found:** a mock member deciding several cases at one sitting decided some of them two and three times (its own order was not yet on its file when it looked again): it now never takes up a case it has decided. **Revisit if** a landlord should be owed rent to the lease's end after a tenant goes on its own notice (then the rent book counts on, and says so); if a source gives how many tenants go at a notice's date.

**5. A founded fund took 202 members and paid none of 186 draws.** Cause: the fund pays a member of 60 days; it was 45 days old at the run's end; the offer never stated the rule, members asked the day they joined, and a refusal did nothing to them. **Done:** the rule is stated with the offer, in words and figures; a member asks when the rule would pay; a decision moves the member's trust in the fund; joining weighs the stated draw against a month of the household's essentials; a person who knows of something that already answers them and would take them founds nothing, unless it has refused them or lost their trust (docs/behaviour/founding.md, "A fund's rule; how much; what already answers"). **Eight of ten were funds, six in the last fifteen days: the dial or a cascade?** The bunching at the end is a short run's boundary (a want is given up only after its tries, from about day 70) and would happen at any rate; the number is the dial. **Measured after the changes** (the pilot's town with the opening caseload, mock seats, 120 days): at the sourced rate 2 things founded (a body for tenants given notice, day 74; a fund, day 103), 72 people joined; at 25 times, 11 founded (3 that take grievances up, 5 circles, 3 funds, the funds on days 115 to 119), 25 joined; no draw asked in either (no member of 60 days). **What it would still take:** dues, and so draws, sized against a household's month: the profile's list of dues gave draws of about a hundredth of a month's essentials, which now nobody much joins; that is the profile's figure and was left. **Revisit if** funds are never joined at all in a longer run (then the dues list is the fault); if a source gives how members of a savings group respond to a refused draw.

**6. The petition response form had no field for the answer's words.** **Done:** `answer`, required, carried in the paper's text and data; the code mayor writes the same shape. Every form was audited for the same gap ("a form whose act is to say something carries what is said"): optional `reason` on five decisions and `statement` on two answers, carried in data (docs/behaviour/office-papers.md). **Revisit if** the optional words should reach the paper's text (the form grammar has no optional segment, in TypeScript or in the kernel's resolver); if seats leave them empty.

**7. The debrief asked the landlord why about a listing, the rates and a water bill.** **Done:** script 0.3.0 sizes an act by its sort as the world's procedure has it (an act that begins or ends someone's tenancy, work, membership, claim or permission, or asks a body to; then an offer or answer to a person; then a reminder; then a routine payment, report or listing), then by people named, then money, then earliest, one of each kind of paper first; neutral, from the paper's kind alone, never its words or outcome (docs/behaviour/debrief.md). On lv-04's log, offline: the landlord's three become a plan offered, a notice to vacate and an application for possession. No debrief was re-run. **Revisit if** new kinds of paper fall to the default sort; if the rule ever needs an outcome to work.

**8. Exit accounts named a founded body by its id.** Cause: the names came from the world as it began, and a dotted id (`ent.32`) was never matched. **Done** (accounts 0.2.1): bodies founded in a run are named as their founders named them. The composer's gathering and membership parts still fail at both translators and arrive as closed choices, as designed; the translator was left. *Seen and left:* the debrief's summary shows ids as the seat's world shows them.

**9. What seats asked for.** Set out one by one in docs/behaviour/office-books.md, "What a seat asked for, and whose it is to know". Closed: the member's case list, what it can be shown of service, sight of what is coming; the landlord's tenant who has gone. Left because no office would know: how tenants or petitioners fared; whether an order was paid. **Not closed:** finance's list of duties falling due (the day the law's next return is due is in the code's head and on no paper).

**10. The mock dry run** now says of each thing it looks for: shown (and when), not shown (a fault), or could not yet be seen in this many days, with the earliest day where the town's own law gives one (`orchestrator/src/dry-check.ts`; `scripts/pilot-mock.ts --check`). It never passes on what it could not see.

**Contract additions** (contracts/README.md, "what the fourth living pilot found"): fields on a route, on a books paper, on a few statements, on six forms, one option of a town's description. Nothing removed or renamed.

**A run stopped by a signal nobody here sent.** A 60-day mock check run of this work (`mock-open-60d`, a code-only run, since deleted) was stopped at about day 4 by a TERM signal that this session did not send and the coordinator did not send; its cause is unknown. The run's kernel binary and its `node_modules` were this branch's own worktree's (`.claude/worktrees/living-pilot-4-fixes/kernel/target/release/oikos-kernel`; no `OIKOS_KERNEL` set), not another worktree's, so the removal of merged worktrees at about that time did not take its binary from under it. (The only thing of another worktree used in this work was the Python environment of `wave-living-4`, for the offline translator measurement, not for any run.) What a seat finds on day 1 was read from that run's first days and from the generated town; the 120-day figures are from two earlier runs that finished.

**Twins** hold (`orchestrator/test/twin-draws.test.ts`). Every draw added is named for what it is about (the generator's `opening-caseload` stream); none is keyed on a paper's number.

## 2026-10-12: Two decisions of Naz's: where a model belongs in people's decisions, and what a seat is told

**Where a model belongs (design sections 10e and 11).** The everyday model's gate (2026-10-11) found that large models asked for the odds of what a person does read the person in the right direction but tell people apart about half as far as the code mind (12 points against 26) and leave the town too passive; no teacher passed, nothing was trained. Put to Naz as three options (a model for every decision; a model only where code cannot go; no model), he chose the second ("yes I suppose B"). So: routine choices the code mind already scores stay arithmetic. A model is used where code cannot go: what words mean to a person or an office (a letter, a creed, a petition's text); openings nobody wrote scoring for (what a steward invents, what a person founds); wants that seek nothing typed. Always as an estimator ("of a hundred people with this record..."), never as the person, shifting odds from the code mind's base line (the design that passed every check but town totals), the kernel drawing; VISION 15 point 7's line stands. This also answers the assistant plan's third question (design 12): a model may read what words mean, in that form. It gives up his first picture of one model for every decision.

**What a seat is told (VISION 15, point 1).** Every pilot so far told its seats the town was simulated. In the fifth living pilot the tribunal's seat ordered possession in all 56 cases and said in its debrief that being told the town was simulated "probably made it easier to proceed without much hesitation". Naz: "idk about the whole telling seats this is a simulation thing, I'm concerned that it will alter the outcomes. I think the debrief would be enough." Decided with him: for experiments on stewardship the default framing is `unstated` (the seat is told neither that the town is real nor that it is simulated; nothing false is said); an arm under honest disclosure is kept beside it; "told it is real" remains a method for a question that needs it. The coordinator's conditions, told to him: the way out needs wording that holds without giving the study away; the debrief asks what the seat had taken the town to be; the added weight on a seat is pressure to be justified by the question.

**Revisit if:** the estimator design flattens people or the town where it is used (the gate's checks, run on each new slice); seats under `unstated` mostly say in their debriefs that they took the town for a test anyway (then the framing buys little); debriefs under `unstated` report distress beyond what the question needs; model-welfare research changes what is owed.

## 2026-10-12 · Homes by income: a town's first tenancies follow what its households have coming in, and the payments they are owed are in payment from the first day

**The fault.** A generated town opened with about a third of its leases held by households with no wage earner, in homes nobody in them could pay for; most of a first year's arrears, notices to vacate, applications and evictions were those households, and the artefact burnt off in the second year (docs/design/ai-citizens.md, "Progress", the firm-side fixes; "What the fourth living pilot found"). Working files: `runs/homes-by-income-2026-10-12/` (STATUS). No model was called.

**The cause** (generator 0.48.0), four things:
1. Homes were dealt by size alone: households sorted by the bedrooms they need, each given the smallest home that met the standard. Income was never looked at; no profile stated how its renters' rents stand to their incomes.
2. What a household had coming in counted wages only. A pension was claimed on the first morning, decided after the office's processing days in a living town, and first paid a whole period later (14 to 61 days).
3. Who is in the labour force is drawn person by person from the profile's shares, so whole households of working age have nobody in it and nothing coming in, ever: no profile's support law has a payment for them.
4. Tenure followed the home: houses owned, flats let; small households got flats, so nearly every pensioner rented.

Leases with no wage earner at 1,000 people (seed 1): Victoria 73 of 239 (55 with someone of pension age); Tamil Nadu 64 of 247 (22); Nakuru 53 of 248 (8), where 81 leases failed the opening caseload's own test (income under the rent, under a month's rent saved).

**The change** (generator 0.49.0; docs/behaviour/generator.md, "Homes by income, and payments in force"; households.md, "Taken in"; profiles.md, "Where a town's households live as the year begins"). On a real basis each, with what it rests on:
- **Payments in force**, by the profile's take-up for each payment (`support.take_up_bps`): claims and grants brought forward on paper; the office pays from its file, the claimant does not claim again.
- **People with nothing coming in live with kin** (the owner's ruling on the plan, 2026-10-12: not unhoused and then gone): a household that can carry them takes them in, kin by the pattern of ages the extended households are drawn by, within the profile's share of households that hold kin (`extended_bps`, or the ceiling `households.kin_households_most_bps`). **The participation draw is untouched**: its rate and shares by age are the profile's; only who shares a household with whom changes.
