## 2026-10-13 · Culture: the cost of carrying the section (step 0 of steps 4 and 5; no model called)

Steps 1 to 3 reported that a run with the dial on is 2.3% to 2.8% slower, nearly all of it "the record carrying the section", against a design budget far lower (design 14i). Traced, and the section made smaller.

- **The mechanism.** The kernel canonicalises a person's whole merged record to check its size, merges it again, canonicalises it a second time and hashes it, at every `entity_record` command, whichever section moved (`kernel/crates/world/src/kernel.rs`, `precheck` and `apply_prechecked`). A section therefore costs its bytes at every write of the record, moved or not. The log carries only the changed section, so it is not what grows. The participant side was already right: the section is worked out again only when a picture has moved or 30 days have gone, an unchanged one is the same array and is neither compared nor written.
- **Measured the way that resolves it.** A whole-run timing cannot: identical runs on this shared machine differ by about 4% (interleaved off/on, four pairs, 60 days of the 1,000-person town: old shape +1.0%, positional +0.9% by the best of four, and +0.0% by the mean of four for both). So the kernel's record writes were timed alone (a counter around the `entity_record` command in a throwaway copy, not committed): they are 2.9% of a run (630 ms of 22 s, 14,620 writes); with the section as named rows they take 740 ms (+16%, which is +0.45% of the run), as positional rows 670 ms (+7%, +0.19% of the run). Three runs of each, spread under 3 ms for the positional and 15 ms for the named. Culture's own computing (hearing, telling, terms) was measured at about 0.25% of the run in steps 1 to 3. **The 2.3% to 2.8% was a noisy whole-run figure; culture costs about 0.5% of a run in all, which is inside the budget (a tenth).**
- **What was changed.** `norms` is positional: the place in the closed conduct list is the conduct, a row is `[does, approves, own, says, n]` or `null`, trailing nulls left off. About 120 bytes where named rows were 400 (a quarter of a 1,700-byte record); a record with the section is 16% bigger than one without, where it was 32%. Content is the same; `normsRows` reads it as named rows. Contract: `entity-record.schema.json` (logged in contracts/README.md); no log of the old shape exists outside the day's own runs. Dial off: nothing changed.
- **The floor, and what would remove it.** With no culture at all the writes cost 630 ms in 22 s. If the kernel kept each section's canonical bytes with the record (the direct writer and `canonical_members` already exist for the state's records), a write would pay for what it changed, not for the record, and every section of every record would be cheaper. That is a kernel change; not made here. Step 5 adds a second section (what a person remembers of the town), kept as small for the same reason.

**Revisit if** a town of 10,000 spends noticeably more of its time in record writes (then make the kernel change, whose value grows with sections added), or a further section is added without being kept to a few hundred bytes.

## 2026-10-13 · Culture, step 4: what a tie's act is to me, what I say, children and newcomers (no model called, no pilot)

Built behind the dial (off: nothing changes; `culture-dial.test.ts`, the living, reading and twin-draws tests pass). Doc: docs/behaviour/culture.md, "What a tie's act is to me", "Children and newcomers", "The lean at the choices that had no record".

- **Visible to a tie** is what the tie tells (once, subject to concealment) or what I was there for (step 5). No third way, so no act is counted twice and no register is read.
- **Private and expressed views differ by construction.** Told of a tie's act I judge it by what I think (`own`) and feel for the tie by it (cool by up to 500, warm by up to 200, only beyond a margin of 2,500 from the middle); I say what I would *say* (`says`, the arithmetic of `Inner.view`) and only if that is beyond the margin. So a person can cool toward someone and say aloud that what they did is right, and a street can each privately approve and each say "wrong". Shown in `participants/test/culture-step4.test.ts`: twelve who think a conduct right (own 65) and take the street to call it wrong (approves 20) all say "wrong"; thirty rounds of telling each other leave the gap of 45 points where it was; three published readings of a count of seven in ten close it, and they say "right".
- **The cost to the one told** it is held against them is a dent to belonging (up to 300, times a half to one and a half by conformity), a cooler tie to the speaker, and a lower `approves`; approved, a warmer tie. Placeholders; the literature gives directions (Ellickson, Williams, Brennan and Pettit), not amounts.
- **Published counts move `approves` too**: a declared strike ballot's yes share, which was a sighting of `does`, is also what those who voted thought (secret ballot).
- **Children and newcomers.** A parent answers a child's question with how they see things (tenths) and where they come from; at coming of age the child's picture is the parents' mean at `prior_weight`, and their group a parent's. A newcomer (made in the run, no parent here) holds the profile's picture at weight 1 and is drawn a group from the profile's shares (`origin_shares` now travels with the dial). **Departure from 14c:** 14c says a newcomer's group is theirs "own"; the profile gives only the town's shares, not a migrant stream's, so the draw is the town's shares, a marked placeholder. A child born in the run is also "made in the run" and holds its picture lightly until its parents have answered.
- **The lean is recorded** for join, strike (the vote on a ballot for action), complain and take as a decision with `norm` (new decision domains `strike`, `complain`, `take`; contract in contracts/README.md), where steps 1 to 3 recorded it only for choices that already had an outcome. **The term on a want's way** is built: the same lean, times sway, times `way_points` (1,500, a standard deviation of trust or agency) on the `adj` of the union, the tribunal desk (a notice, a debt) and the town's desk. The way and the draw after it are two choices, each swayed once.
- **Not built:** a law as one hearing of approval (a row of 14c that the step-4 list as asked did not include).

**Revisit if** a lone verdict proves too small to matter (sizes are placeholders; the drop condition of 14l is about movement), or the way term and the draw are found to double-count in a measure.

## 2026-10-13 · Culture, step 5: town memory (no model called, no pilot)

Behind the dial (off: nothing changes). Doc: docs/behaviour/culture.md, "Town memory". Code: `participants/src/behaviour/townmemory.ts`, `citizen.ts`. Tests: `participants/test/culture-memory.test.ts`, and a case in `orchestrator/test/no-god-view.test.ts`.

- **Who witnesses, within the no-god-view rule.** The world already shows the departures of a space (who, why, when; the last five) to whoever is inside its building and, from outside, only that someone was seen leaving (`SiteSpace.left`, `seen_leaving`). So the presence route needed no channel, no kernel change and no new act: a person inside a building finds a recent *removed* departure there and has seen a removal; a walk-out is NOT read off departures: the first try (three or more leaving a workplace together in working hours) gave 1,469 walk-outs held in a year of the 1,000-person town with no stoppage in the log, because people leave at all hours (part-timers) and the world shows no cause. Members who stop work hold it as their own and tell it. Only those whose own place puts them there. **A removal in a building next door shows them nothing.**
- **Public by being read, or retold.** The paper's items (law, budget, result, permit decision) for those who read it; a published statement of purpose for a founding; ties retell it one phrase at a catch-up, at 60% of the teller's strength, three hands at most. Nothing is drawn.
- **Fading by a formula, not a pass.** The record row stores the strength on the day it last arrived; the section changes only when something arrives (a year of nothing writes nothing). 30 bytes a slot, six at most.
- **Trust.** A first holding of an event bears once on trust in whoever did it, by the sign of the person's own view of the conduct it shows (a removal is `apply_possession`; held right: the police up; wrong: down; no view: nothing), whether or not they dealt with them. **A view of `apply_possession` is now held wherever the world has a law on possession** (placeholder 5,000), so the sign exists; this adds a row to the norms section.
- **Departures from 14e:** the kinds list is the six something makes public today (`put_out`, `strike`, `ruling`, `law`, `vote`, `founded`; 14e's `let_go_many`, `closed`, `disaster` wait for an occasion people see); a removal's `about` is the police (or the tribunal where there are none), since a bystander cannot tell who carried it out and the world's terms name the doer; strength of a read item is the paper's weight over its heaviest, as 14e says "to 5,000"; commemoration by a founded body (14f) is not built; the told phrase carries the teller's strength in tenths and hands, which 14e leaves open.
- **Not verified:** that a person wakes inside their building often enough to see a removal within `witness_days` (the runs count removals seen against removals carried out).

**Revisit if** removals seen are a small share of removals carried out (then `witness_days` or how often people are home at a wake is the limit, not memory), or strikes are held by too few (only members who stopped work see one).

## 2026-10-13 · Culture, steps 4 and 5 measured: a year of the 1,000-person town, three profiles, five seeds each (nothing tuned; no model)

`oikos run worlds/town-1000.yaml --seeds 5 --until 31536000 --set profile=P --set living.initiative_bps=10000 --set opening_caseload=true --set living.friction_bps=30000 [--set living.culture=true]`, P = au-vic-2026, gb-eng-2026, ke-nakuru-2026; five run seeds of one town each, so the noise is that town's alone. Logs and reports in `runs/culture-2026-10-13/year2/` (outside git; read with `scripts/culture-report.ts`, from the logs alone). The frictions were scaled up threefold and the opening caseload turned on so that removals and tribunal cases occur; they still occurred rarely (about 1.4 removals carried out a year in au-vic, 1.6 in gb-eng, 2.6 in ke-nakuru; no stoppage in any of the 30 runs).

- **Standing measures** (`oikos diff`, `oikos health`): au-vic 0 of 57 beyond 3 standard errors; ke-nakuru 0; gb-eng 1, the union's share of firms in the last month (0.54 to 1.12%, z 5.5), a line that moved identically in the earlier au-vic control with no norm term anywhere (a dial on reshuffles who is told what, not a norm); the gb-eng control was not run. Health breaches: au-vic 4 to 5 (social-group participation 46.2 to 44.6 against a band edge of 45; the runs' ranges overlap), gb-eng 4 to 5 (demand unmet 5.4), ke-nakuru 2 to 2. Nothing says a norm moved a measure.
- **Norms** (mean over people of each person's number, day 7 to day 364, mean over the five runs, three profiles). `take_in` `does` falls 5.3, 7.2 and 4.9 points (50 to about 45): the only conduct whose picture moves by more than a point in every profile, and it moves because people who were asked and said no are told (a conduct with a marked placeholder start, no rate of its own). ke-nakuru `complain` `does` +1.5. Every other `does` and `approves` is within 0.2 of where it started (`approves` for `take_in` -0.2 at most), in all three profiles. **`approves` stays at 50 for everyone** to within a few tenths, though the spread of `approves` across people grows from 0 to 0.4-1.2 for the conducts told of: nothing is expressed because nothing is done often enough to be told and judged. `own` drifts 17 to 14 in spread (it settles toward `approves`, half in three years: that is internalisation working, not the street).
- **Said against thought:** the mean gap between what people think and what they say of a conduct is 10.1 to 10.2 points in every profile (people vary 17 in what they think, and say within 3.7 of the middle: `says` is `own` pulled toward `approves`). That is the said/thought gap of Kuran as built; it exists everywhere and drives nothing yet because nothing it hides is anything people act on.
- **Verdicts** (step 4's expressed disapproval or approval of an act told): 0.2 to 0.6 a town a year. Of an act told to someone who then holds it beyond the margin (2,500 from the middle): their `own` is 50 +- 17, so about 14% of hearers could (either side), and acts told are tens a year.
- **Town memory** (step 5): 66 to 79% of people hold at least one event at day 364, 2.3 to 2.8 slots each. In au-vic and gb-eng nearly all are what the paper reported (`vote` 1,400 to 1,500 and `law` 700 to 1,100 holdings, about 58% read, the rest told by one or two hands). In ke-nakuru fewer holdings are read (807 against 1,100 to 1,500) and more are told, and **removals travel**: about 2.6 carried out a year, 120 holdings by sight, 2,603 told, **some through three hands** (406). **A story:** ke-nakuru, seed 1, a household put out by the police on day 58. Fifteen people who were in the building when it happened saw it and now take landlords to apply for possession more than others do (the share they think is done: 61 against 50.6 for the 574 who never heard of it). By the end of the year 75 had it from someone who saw it, 185 through a second hand, 193 through a third: 453 of 1,067 people hold it, 574 do not. About 450 who never dealt with the police now carry some trust in them (the event created it, once, by each one's own view of the conduct): of the 574 who hold nothing of it, 132 have any (mean 3,750 of 10,000), of the 15 who saw it 15 have, at 3,160 (lower, for those who hold a removal wrong). A year on, those who saw it hold it at half the strength they first did.
- **Log and speed.** Compressed logs, mean of five runs: au-vic 412 MB off, 414 on (+0.5%); gb-eng 400, 406 (+1.5%); ke-nakuru 412, 411 (-0.2%). Run time: whole-run seconds in these batches are not comparable (the machine's load varied from 172 to 385 s for the same run); in three interleaved pairs of 60 days at the end, user CPU time best of three was 30.59 s off and 31.05 s on (+1.5%), the means 31.35 and 31.73 (+1.2%), the real times 22.86 and 22.96 (+0.4%): about 1%, inside the noise of a shared machine, and inside 14i's tenth.
- **The drop condition of 14l** ("norms move less than the spread between seeds"), per conduct. Read exactly, the mean of a number over a thousand people differs between run seeds of one town by only 0.1 to 0.5 points, so a shift of two tenths is "more than the seeds differ" and the test says little. Read by what matters (a shift of a point or more): **still met for `answer_tribunal`, `stay_past_notice`, `take_to_tribunal`, `join_union`, `strike`, `take_from_employer`, `apply_possession` (their `does` and `approves` do not move), and for `approves` of every conduct; not met for `take_in` `does` in all three profiles, and for ke-nakuru `complain` `does`.** `join_union` `does` stays at its calibrated 13 to 19 while the spread across people grows to about 3: some people drift either way, the town's mean does not.
- **Why I think it is still met (without changing a size to fix it).** (1) **Too few visible acts for a town of this size and length**: a conduct's occasions are tens a year in a town of 1,000, each told to a few of the 15 people one catches up with, and one told act moves a `does` by 1 over the weight held (4 to 20) so about a tenth of the way; to move a mean by a point the town needs hundreds of tellings of the same side. The two conducts that move are the ones with many occasions (`take_in` asks) or many people (`complain` in ke-nakuru). (2) **Effect sizes**: a verdict needs a hearer more than 25 points from the middle on a conduct (about 14% of people), and moves `approves` by 1 over `n`+1. (3) **A missing route**: removals and strikes, the events people would see, are rare here (a stoppage never occurred in 30 runs); and `approves` is only ever moved by what is said of an act, which needs the act first. What would test it without a size changed: a town of 10,000 or two years, or a scenario in which the events occur (dear rents with a jobs slump). Not done here.
- **Not verified:** the control with the dial on and no norm term for gb-eng and ke-nakuru; the walk-out and founding routes of town memory at scale (no stoppage and no founded body read in these runs); what a removal does to `stay_past_notice` and `answer_tribunal` in the town that sees one (ke-nakuru's `stay_past_notice` `does` +0.8 is the only trace).

**Revisit if** a longer or larger town is run with the dial on (then read the same table), or a conduct is found to need more occasions than a year gives it (then it is a measure to read at a longer length, not a size to change).

## 2026-10-13 · Culture: why `approves` never moves (diagnosis only; no model, no code fault found, nothing changed in the arithmetic)

The question: `approves` is 50 for everyone in every run of the 1,000-person town, and `does` moves for two conducts only. Is that a fault? Method: counters on every route (written, delivered, read, applied, kept in the record), temporary and not committed (a patch, kept outside the repo); `oikos run worlds/town-1000.yaml` / a 3,000-person scale of it (`worlds/town-3000.yaml`, new: citizens, blocks, houses, shops, factories and landlords times three, grid 70 by 52), a year, lean logs, `living.initiative_bps=10000`, `opening_caseload=true`, `living.friction_bps=30000`, `living.culture=true`. Logs deleted after reading; the counts are below.

**Verdict: no fault in wiring, rounding or reading.** Every route is wired end to end and survives to the record the report reads. What stops `approves` is arithmetic that is working as designed, and one scale inherited from another formula (below), which is the owner's to decide, not a fix.

- **Counts, one year, summed over runs** (1,000 au-vic seed 1; 1,000 gb-eng five seeds; 3,000 gb-eng three seeds; 3,000 ke-nakuru three seeds):

| route | 1,000 au (1) | 1,000 gb (5) | 3,000 gb (3) | 3,000 ke (3) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| own acts told (`tell` did-phrases) = heard (`tie.did_heard`) | 921 = 921 | 6,422 = 6,419 | 12,321 = 12,320 | 11,425 = 11,423 |
| a `says` phrase told: own act (not neutral), a matter heard of (not neutral) | 905 (2), 130 | 6,293 (231), 591 | 12,039 (477), 892 | 10,567 (160), 807 |
| `hearSaid` calls by a tie, and those that changed `approves` | 1,035 -> 184 | 6,881 -> 1,101 | 12,930 -> 1,959 | 11,364 -> 1,210 |
| voice defined (a verdict sent) = received = applied | 0 | 1 | 12 | 13 |
| tie cooled or warmed (`react.tie`) | 79 | 658 | 1,271 | 1,052 |
| published ballot count (`approves` and `does`) | 0 | 0 | 11 | 4 |
| `does` updates by a tie, and changed | 905 -> 905 | 6,328 -> 6,328 | 11,893 -> 11,893 | 11,347 -> 11,347 |
| `does` by being there (a removal seen) | 0 | 56 | 74 | 2,198 |
| household (child coming of age) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

  Every message told is heard; every hearing is applied; no update was rounded to nothing (`does`: all changed; `approves`: the rest are hearings of 5,000 on 5,000, which move nothing because nothing is there to move). The record keeps what moved: at the end of a year the mean of the true figure and of the figure in the record differ by 0.00 points for `approves` and at most 0.4 for `does` (the grain of 2 percent leaves 2 people in a thousand a point off on one conduct), so the report reads the right field and sees what is there.
- **Why `approves` stays at 50: four things, in order of weight.**
  1. **Almost nobody says anything but "neither right nor wrong".** What a person says is their own view moved toward what they take to be approved, by `belonging x (1 - integrity) x 4` (0 to 1). That `4` is the scale of `Inner.view`, where the pressure is a product of three fractions (how much they could cost me, how afraid I am, how little I trust them) and rarely near 1. Here the factor is the single weight of belonging (0 to 1, about 0.5), so the gap saturates: **57% of people have a gap of exactly 1** (they say exactly what they take the street to approve) and the rest keep about a fifth of the distance between their view and it (mean kept 0.12 of 1 over everyone; 846 people measured, `join_union`). `says` ranges over about 43 to 57 (a spread of 3 against 17 in what they think), which falls in the middle step of the five sayings ("neither right nor wrong", 40 to 60) for 97 to 99% of people. A person who says what the street already approves tells the street nothing: this is Kuran's preference falsification at its fixed point, in code, and a street that starts at 50 stays at 50.
  2. **The verdict route is almost unreachable.** A verdict is voiced only if what is *said* sits more than 25 points from the middle. Said is squeezed as above: a person with a gap of g says at most 50 x (1 - g) points from the middle even for a view of 0 or 100, so 25 needs a gap of a half or less and an extreme view. Voice was defined 0 times in the 1,000 au-vic year and once in five gb-eng years; 12 and 13 times at 3,000.
  3. **A neutral hearing pulls back.** About 85% of the hearings are of 5,000, and each is a pull toward 50 that undoes the last non-neutral one (`approves` moves by (5,000 - held) over `n` + 1). That is the cancel the question asked about: it is the design (what others say is what is approved), and it is working.
  4. **The mean cannot move, whatever the spread.** Every person starts at the profile's `approves` (no profile gives one, so 5,000 everywhere) and holds a view that is that figure plus a symmetric spread. What is said, then, is symmetric around the start; the mean of what a town takes to be approved is a martingale. It moves only through an asymmetry the profile would give (a group's own figures, `approves_bps` in `dials.culture.profile.by_origin`: no profile has one) or an event that is one-sided. What does move is the **spread across people**, 0 at the start to 0.4-1.2 points (au-vic, gb-eng), 1.1 for `take_in` and up to 0.8 for `join_union` at 3,000. `culture-report.ts sum`'s drop condition compares a *mean* shift with the seeds' spread; for `approves` it cannot be met by construction. Read the spread across people (`people_sd_end`).
- **An experiment that is not a change** (one run, au-vic, seed 1, 1,000 people, a year; the `4` set to `1` by a variable in a counter patch, not committed): the gap is no longer saturated, 34 verdicts are voiced (0 before), `approves` is changed 1,604 times by ties and 34 by verdicts (181 and 0 before), `take_in` `approves` is not 50 for 475 people (range 35 to 63; 66 before, 44 to 58), `join_union` 191 (34 to 68); the town's *mean* is still 50 +- 0.1, as it must be. So the scale is what keeps the street silent, and the answer to "does it then move" is "the spread does, the mean does not". **Not applied.** It is a size, and changing it to produce movement is against the rule; it needs the owner's word, and a name of its own (`say_gap_scale`, now a literal in `Culture.says`) if it is to be a parameter at all.
- **`does` on the conducts that did not move: too few occasions in the 1,000-person town, not a fault.** Counts of own acts told in a year: 1,000 au-vic (one run): `answer_tribunal` 0, `take_to_tribunal` 0, `strike` 0, `complain` 1, `stay_past_notice` 2, `take_from_employer` 4, `join_union` 102, `take_in` 142 (no yes). 1,000 gb-eng (five runs): `answer_tribunal` 0, `take_to_tribunal` 0, `strike` 0, `stay_past_notice` 3, `take_from_employer` 17, `join_union` 404, `take_in` 1,465 (27 yes). The tribunal, the ballot and the writing of a complaint do not come up in a year in a town of 1,000 even with the frictions threefold and the opening caseload on, and nothing a person does not do can be told. Where occasions exist the figure moves and every sighting changes it (`does` changes on every hearing). At 3,000 ke-nakuru the same conducts have occasions (`answer_tribunal` 103 acts told, `stay_past_notice` 288, `complain` 125 over three runs).
- **A town of 3,000 (gb-eng and ke-nakuru, three seeds each, a year).** The picture is the same at three times the occasions, with more of everything. `approves`: mean within 0.1 of 50 for every conduct; spread across people 0 to 1.1. `does`: `take_in` -6.4 (gb), -4.9 (ke), as at 1,000 (a conduct with a placeholder start and nobody yes to tell); ke-nakuru, where removals are common and seen (2,198 sightings; about 250 holdings by sight in a run; about 1.3 stoppages a run), `stay_past_notice` +1.1, `apply_possession` +1.0, `complain` +1.4 (at 1,000: +0.8, +0.1, +1.5); gb-eng, where removals are rarer, nothing else moves by a point. A published ballot count reached 11 hearers in gb-eng and 4 in ke-nakuru (the strikes that ran): `strike` `does` stays at its 85. So scale helps a conduct whose occasion is visible and frequent, and not one that is rare; that is as expected, and nothing shows a fault.
- **The control** (gb-eng, five seeds of one 1,000-person town, a year; `oikos diff`): dial off, dial on at default, dial on with `sway_milli` 0, and dial on with no conduct at all (`conducts: []`, so only origin groups, homophily and the phrase "I come from the X group" remain). The union's share of firms in the last month: **0.54 off, 0.96 on with groups only (z 2.3), 1.12 on with the norm term at 0, 1.12 on at default**. The norm term and the default are the same (z < 1 between them, and no measure moves beyond 3 standard errors between sway 0 and default); the shift is the dial's other parts, about three quarters of it already present with groups and homophily and no norm at all, the rest within the noise. **It moves because of the groups and the talk they add (who is told what), not the norm term.** This matches the earlier au-vic control (no norm term anywhere), and says the finding at 1,000 and gb-eng is a reshuffling, not culture.
- **What a town of this size lacks (a finding for the owner, nothing built).** In a real town people talk about others' conduct all the time, not only when a rare event has happened: who is behind on the rent, who is doing well, who is cold to a neighbour. Gossip is how a street learns what is acceptable (Dunbar 1996, *Grooming, Gossip and the Evolution of Language*, **to confirm**; Dunbar, Marriott and Duncan 1997, "Human conversational behavior", *Human Nature* 8(3), **to confirm**: about two thirds of conversation is social topics; Gluckman 1963, "Gossip and scandal", *Current Anthropology* 4(3), **to confirm**). Here a person tells an act only if there was an occasion in the last `news_days`, and says what they think only of an act they have heard, so there is almost nothing to say and what is said is the street's own opinion. What would make approval visible: (1) a standing voice about conduct that is not tied to a rare event, a person's ordinary opinion of what a neighbour does, said to those they are close to (where the saturation above is lower: one says what one thinks to a friend), (2) the said/thought gap by tie closeness rather than one figure for everyone, (3) the gap's scale being the product-of-three scale it was borrowed from, and (4) profile figures for what is approved, by group, where a source gives them (step 8). None is built; (3) is a one-line change the owner may want to see in a run first.
- **Honest view.** As built, in a town of 1,000 to 3,000 and a year, culture can show: a town's memory of a public event and its travel (it works), `does` for a conduct whose occasion is frequent and visible, and a spread across people in what they take the street to approve. It cannot show a shift in what a town approves, because the mean cannot move on its own and the spread is the whole signal. Two years or 10,000 people multiply the occasions, not the saturation. The route to a visible approval is a change of kind (1 to 4 above), not of length.

**Changed:** `scripts/culture-report.ts` takes an optional world file (`run <log> <profile> <seed> [world.yaml]`), for the 3,000-person town; `worlds/town-3000.yaml` added. Nothing in a run is changed: dial off is the world it was (the dial tests are unaffected; no source of a run was edited).

**Revisit if** the gap scale becomes a parameter or the voice is given a place in ordinary talk (then read the spread of `approves` across people, not its mean), a profile gives approval figures by group (then the mean can differ from 50 and the report's drop condition is meaningful), or removals prove common enough in another profile for `apply_possession` to be seen by hundreds.


## 2026-10-14 · Culture: the gap between thought and said, where people start, ordinary talk about others (three commits; measured once; nothing tuned afterwards; no model)

The finding of "why `approves` never moves" (2026-10-13) named three causes. Each is a commit, with tests, its reasoning and basis in docs/behaviour/culture.md, sources in docs/research/references.md. Dial off: byte-identical to main (`culture-dial`, living, reading and twin-draws tests all pass; generator version and goldens unchanged). No contract changed except additions logged in contracts/README.md; no kernel change; seats' instructions, the translator's prompt and forms unchanged.

**1. The gap scale (a mistake, not a calibration).** What a person said of a conduct was their own view moved toward the street's by `belonging x (1 - integrity) x 4`. The 4 came from `Inner.view`, where the pressure is a product of three fractions and rarely near 1; here the factor was a single weight, so it saturated at 1 for 57% of people. Now `pressure = R / (R + I)`, `R = reputation_scale_milli/1000 x belonging x conformity`, `I = integrity`, `says = own + pressure x (approves - own)`: Kuran's balance of the reputation lost by standing out against the inner cost of misstating one's view, each cost taken as growing with the square of its distance (our reading of the form, to confirm against the book). Meaning of the scale: the share of the way to the street's view that is gone aloud; 0 for one who does not care or has all integrity, 1 for one with none, a half where the two weigh alike. `reputation_scale_milli` (1,000, the two weighing alike when belonging, conformity and integrity are all 1) is a parameter. It was derived, not picked for its effect: the typical person (all at a half) has a pressure of a third, the order of the third of critical Asch trials that conformed (Asch 1956; Bond and Smith 1996, to confirm). Five existing test cases that relied on saturation were given the person who really is saturated (belonging 1, conformity 1, integrity 0 to 0.05); one had stated the old premise that a street leaks nothing, which is now only true of such people.

**2. Where people start.** All nine profiles now carry `approves_bps` for four conducts (answer and take a wrong to the tribunal: confidence in the courts; write to the town: confidence in the civil service; join the union: confidence in unions), from their own `outlook.trust` (World Values Survey / European Values Study wave 7 as Our World in Data publishes it, opened 2026-10-11, to confirm), with the mapping and its weakness in `sources["culture.conducts"]`. **How sure: low.** Confidence in an institution is not approval of an act toward it; the share above a threshold is read as a mean, as `outlook` does; national, not the place's. No figure for `strike`, `take_in`, `stay_past_notice`, `take_from_employer` or the organisations' conducts (the survey items on joining strikes and on justifying stealing were not opened); no figure by origin group (none found), so `by_group` is empty and no group differs at the start. Those conducts start from values alone, as before. The figure is the start of both the picture and the lean, measured from it, so calibrated rates hold. A limit that remains by construction: with one figure for both, the mean of what is said stays its start unless an asymmetry exists (a group whose figure differs, a count from outside).

**3. Ordinary talk.** Asked how things are (the catch-up that exists), a person may add one phrase of one act of a third person that the third person told them first-hand and what they say of it; `learnOf` is called only from the first-person phrase, so nobody tells of someone who did not tell them; never of the asker; once to each asker; 180 days; eight people kept; not re-told. The hearer: one sighting along the tie, the said view as what is approved (`hearSaid`), `noteHeard`, and `react` toward the one talked about if that person is a tie (a stranger's act moves the picture and creates no tie). One draw (`culture-gossip`), made only when there is something to tell. Rates are placeholders fixed before any run and not adjusted: `gossip_bps` 3,000, `gossip_days` 180, `third_kept` 8, basis in culture.md (Dunbar et al. 1997 and the others, to confirm). A no-god-view case holds it.

**Measured once** (`scripts/culture-3-batch.sh`, `scripts/culture-report.ts`; a year; frictions threefold and `opening_caseload` on; dial off against on; logs deleted after reading, `runs/culture-3/rep` kept outside git). 1,000 people, au-vic / gb-eng / ke-nakuru, five seeds each; 3,000 people, gb-eng / ke-nakuru, three seeds each.
- **Does approval move?** In the mean, no, within a point: the four sourced conducts end where they began (`answer_tribunal` 59.0 to 59.0, 65.0 to 65.0, 50.0 to 50.0; `join_union` 29.0 to 28.6, 35.0 to 34.0, 42.0 to 41.4; `complain` 48.0 to 48.0, 51.0 to 51.0, 45.0 to 44.7; at 3,000 the same, `join_union` gb 35.0 to 33.4 the largest). The mean of what is said is a martingale around its start, as stated above, and nothing asymmetric was given. In **spread across people**, `approves` now varies where it used to be 0: `take_in` 3.7 to 4.5 points (sd), `join_union` 2.0 to 2.8, ke-nakuru `complain` 2.5 and `answer_tribunal` 1.7, `stay_past_notice` 1.8 (the conducts whose occasions are seen); `answer_tribunal` in au-vic and gb-eng 0 to 0.1 (nothing occurs to make anyone differ). `does` moves as before where occasions are frequent and seen (`take_in` -9 to -13 from its placeholder start; ke-nakuru `complain` +3.8 at 1,000, +3.4 at 3,000), and nowhere else by a point.
- **What did change.** Verdicts voiced a year: 0 to 13 before, now au-vic 74, gb-eng 48, ke-nakuru 26 at 1,000, and 268 and 70 at 3,000 (gb, ke). The share of people who said something other than "neither right nor wrong": 25 to 87% by conduct (was 1 to 3%). Tales told of a third person's conduct: about 1,550 (au), 2,000 (gb), 1,680 (ke) a year at 1,000; 5,900 (gb) and 4,770 (ke) at 3,000. The gap between thought and said averages 4 points (own sd 16 to 17). Pluralistic ignorance (privately on one side by more than 5 points, taking the street to be on the other by more than 5): where a profile's figure sits far from the middle, 11 to 20% at the start of `answer_tribunal`, `take_to_tribunal` and `join_union` in au-vic and gb-eng, 23% for ke-nakuru `join_union`, falling by 3 to 7 points over the year as talk spreads what is said; 0 where the figure is 50. Ties: 0.2 to 0.3 cooled ties kept per person at the end of the year (resented), against none in the first week.
- **Standing measures** (`oikos diff`; `oikos health`). 1,000: 0 of 57 beyond 3 standard errors in all three profiles; the largest are -2.7 (au-vic participation_pct, 60.5 to 60.2), -2.5 (gb-eng took_part_pct) and +2.6 (ke-nakuru overcrowded households). Health breaches identical off and on (4, 4, 2). 3,000 ke-nakuru: 0 of 67 beyond; **3,000 gb-eng: 4 of 67 beyond with three seeds** (a religious group's affiliation z -4.9 and its first-time firm share +3.6, households apart 0.7 to 3.0, median rent 20.1 to 21.0%); health breaches the same (5 and 5). Three seeds make the standard errors small, and the earlier control (gb-eng, 2026-10-13) showed that this dial's other parts (groups, homophily, the talk they add) already reshuffle such lines with no norm term; no control was run here and none of these is chased (record, don't chase). Nothing says a norm moved a measure.
- **Speed and log.** 1,000, five runs in parallel: 214 to 228 s (au-vic, +6%), 229 to 233 (gb-eng, +2%), 247 to 256 (ke-nakuru, +4%) a run, best read as +2 to 6% on a shared machine; log (compressed) +1.4%, +0.1%, +2.5% (about 1.3 GB for five runs). 3,000: no slowdown beyond noise (gb-eng 1,057 to 1,025 s; ke-nakuru 903 to 825 s, a run's mean); log -1.2%, -1.4% (noise). Dial on costs about as much as before the three changes.
- **A story** (gb-eng, 1,000 people, seed 1). On days 56 and 57 c0429 told two people it knows, c0511 and c0486, that c0907 had said no to someone who asked for a roof, and added that it was wrong. Both held the placeholder 50 on what households do and 50 on what would be called right at day 55. On day 81 each held that 33 in 100 take people in and that 56 in 100 would call taking in right (other tellings had reached them in between, so not all of it is c0429's), and c0511's own view is 32, c0486's 45. The conduct's start is the placeholder, which is why the move is large; nothing is known to be wrong with this person's behaviour.

**What I am unsure of.** (1) Squared costs in the gap rule: Kuran leaves the form open and I chose the one that gives a share. (2) Courts, civil service and unions' confidence as stand-ins for approval of acts is weak, and the mean not moving is an honest result of giving no source for an asymmetry; it would move with group figures. (3) `take_in` `does` moving by -9 to -13 is a placeholder start and nobody saying yes in a year, as before; not a finding. (4) The 3,000 gb-eng measures.

**Revisit if** a source gives approval by group or an item that is not confidence (the survey's own items on strikes, stealing; a national survey of attitudes to using the courts), which would give the mean something to move from; the supply of acts to tell of grows (more occasions, or acts seen), when `gossip_bps` may be worth reading against a diary study of everyday talk; or the said view becomes cheap enough to depend on the tie (to a friend one says more of what one thinks).

## 2026-10-14 · Culture, steps 6 and 7: an office's practice kept and reachable but never handed over; measures read from logs (the proof run of step 9 not yet run; no model)

**Step 6.** The owner ruled (2026-10-13) that a seat is not shown its office's past practice as ready counts. Built: `participants/src/behaviour/practice.ts` and `Org.grants`: a code organisation keeps, in its own record's new `practice` section, for hold / rise / stay: occasions, yeses, since (counts roll over 1,825 days); it opens with 100 occasions at the rate its character gives (computed, no draw, generator unchanged); with the dial on and 5 occasions, its rate moves half way (`practice_inertia_bps`) toward its habit relative to its character's rate, so at the opening nothing moves. All sizes placeholders, in culture.md, basis Nelson and Winter, Lipsky, Stinchcombe (to confirm). A seat gets nothing added: it looks through its office's own files by kind and date (the existing `look`; bounded, a turn of the sitting). Tests: practice outlasts a window and a change of holder (given the record), a bounded section, no part of what a seat is shown reads practice, prompt byte-identical dial on and off, another office's files refused (contract example `files-of-another-office.json`, no-god-view case). **Not built:** a time cost for the search (shared sitting clock; proposed); counting a seat's replies as practice; a code holder reading its own record mid-run (no module is shown it). No translator, instruction or debrief change; debrief wording proposed in culture.md. **Revisit if** a seat does not think to look (instructions would then need a line, the owner's call).

**Step 7.** `orchestrator/src/culture-measures.ts`, through `oikos pilot-report` and `oikos dataset` (`culture.json`); documented in culture.md. Tipping events (defined before any run) need decisions, so a full log.

**Step 9 not run; what was found.** Exploration only (1,000 people, 140 days, one seed): a market demand collapse from day 75 changed nothing; from day 0 it produced strike ballots, published counts and a stoppage; removals stay at zero warrants even with dear rents and frictions x10. So of the three shocks, only one (a demand collapse from day 0, giving layoffs, a strike and a published ballot count) bites by configuration; a wave of removals does not, and nothing can be timed to month three. The criteria are in `runs/c4/STATUS`. A 3,000-person proof is 40 runs, each producing a log of many GB on a shared, full disk: it needs its own session with the disk to itself. **Revisit:** run it once removals can be provoked (a mechanic or a policy parameter the owner approves).

## 2026-10-14 · Culture, step 9: the proof run (shocked against unshocked towns, a year; measurement only: no run code, size, rate or threshold changed; no model, no pilot)

**Criteria, fixed before any run** (copied verbatim from `runs/c4/STATUS` into `runs/culture-proof/STATUS`, with how they apply to the reduced design written there before the first run). A shock *bites* if its event count (ballots + published counts + stoppages) is at least 1.5 times the unshocked town's and beyond the seed spread. Culture *responds* if, for both profiles and paired by seed over at least five seeds: **R1** a conduct the shock touches differs in mean does/approves/says by more than 2 points and by more than 2 sd of the paired differences; **R2** holders of the relevant remembered event differ from non-holders by more than 2 points more in the shocked arm; **R3** verdicts or tales are more than 20% higher beyond seed spread; **R4** holders' trust in the party moved by at least 200 bps more than others'. Not responding: every difference inside 2 sd of the paired seeds. Fixed for the reduced design: R1's conducts are `strike`, `join_union`, `take_from_employer`; R2's event is `strike`; the verdict is read from the 1,000-person arm (five seeds), the 3,000-person arm (three seeds) cannot meet ">= 5 seeds" and is corroboration.

**What ran.** `shocks=[{"from_day":0,"kind":"goods","what":"demand","factor_bps":300}]` (the exploration's shock), friction x3, opening caseload, initiative 10,000, a year, `scripts/slots.ts`. 1,000 people, gb-eng and au-vic, five seeds, shocked and unshocked, dial on (20 runs); gb-eng dial off, five seeds, shocked and unshocked (10 runs); 3,000 people, gb-eng and ke-nakuru, three seeds, shocked and unshocked, dial on (12 runs). **42 runs, nothing cut.** The 1,000-person runs kept a full log with decisions (so tipping events could be read); the 3,000-person runs a lean log (no decisions, so no tipping at 3,000). Each log was read once by `scripts/culture-proof.ts` (the step 7 measures plus event counts) into a small file, then deleted; `scripts/culture-proof-sum.ts` pairs the arms; `oikos diff` reads the standing measures. All outputs are in `runs/culture-proof/` (outside git). The same town is run in each batch (run seeds apart), so the noise is that town's. Disk: 137 GB free at the start, never under 108 GB, 128 GB at the end.

**What the shock did to the town** (it is a very large shock: employment to population 62% to 14.5% in gb-eng, 60% to 27% in au-vic, 49% to 8% and 66% to 19% at 3,000; `oikos diff` 28 to 34 measures beyond 3 standard errors, all of them the economy, rents and who goes to gatherings). Bite: **gb-eng 1,000: 10.2 events against 3.0 (bites), strike ballots 3.0 against 0.0, stoppages 1.2 against 0.0. au-vic 1,000: 4.8 against 3.4 (1.4 times, inside the spread: does not bite).** 3,000: gb-eng 17.0 against 12.7 (1.3 times, does not bite; stoppages 2.7 against 0.3 do); ke-nakuru 46.0 against 9.3 (bites). Warrants carried out (removals): no difference in any town (1 to 2 a year).

**R1, the picture.** Not met in any town. At day 364, shocked minus unshocked: `strike` does 85.0 and approves 50.0 in both arms (differences 0.0 to -0.1); `take_from_employer` 1.0 and 50.0, no difference; `join_union` does -0.6 (gb-eng, sd of pairs 0.4), -0.4 (au-vic, 0.5), -0.2 (gb-eng 3,000), -0.3 (ke-nakuru 3,000); `join_union` approves -0.7 (gb-eng, beyond 2 sd, sd 0.3), -0.4 (au-vic, beyond 2 sd, sd 0.1), -0.4 and +0.2 at 3,000 (inside). Beyond 2 sd, but under a point, nowhere near the 2 points. It builds slowly and is still growing at year end (gb-eng `join_union` does: -0.1 at day 210, -0.3 at 270, -0.6 at 364), so it did not "last" in the sense of a peak; there is no peak. A likelier cause than the norm is that fewer people changed job in the shocked town, so fewer occasions to join (see the faults below), but the dial-off arm records no norms, so this cannot be separated. Spread across people of `approves` grows more where the shock acted (gb-eng `strike` approves sd 0.9 against 0.0 at day 364, beyond 2 sd; `join_union` +0.5): some people moved, the mean did not.

**R2, near against far.** Not met. Holders of a remembered strike against others, at day 364 (the calm arm has almost none, so the comparison is against zero): gb-eng 1,000 (two of five seeds had a picture at day 364) does +0.6, approves +0.8, says +1.4, own +1.7; gb-eng 3,000 (355 holders a run) does +0.3, approves +0.3, says +0.7, own +1.0; ke-nakuru 3,000 (135 holders) does +0.7, approves +1.1, says -0.1, own -1.0. All under 2 points and inside the pairs' sd. The strike does not reach `does` or `approves` for anyone, near or far (see the faults).

**R3, talk.** Met for verdicts in both profiles: voiced verdicts a year gb-eng 102 against 48 (+112%, sd of pairs 25), au-vic 132 against 74 (+78%, sd 20); 3,000: gb-eng 347 against 268 (+29%, sd 57, inside), ke-nakuru 86 against 71 (inside). Tales of third persons' acts: gb-eng +17% (beyond 2 sd, under 20%), au-vic +9% (inside), gb-eng 3,000 +15% (beyond), ke-nakuru +6% (inside). **But au-vic did not bite and still shows the larger rise in verdicts**, and verdicts are of acts told ("At a new job: I joined / did not join"): the extra talk follows the churn in jobs the shock causes, not the stoppages. Standing: people told "right" of an act 51 against 24 (gb-eng, beyond 2 sd), 61 against 37 (au-vic), 162 against 120 (gb 3,000, beyond); told "wrong" 15 against 8, 13 against 7 (inside). Ties cooled per person at year end 0.84 against 0.30 (gb-eng), 0.66 against 0.38 (au-vic), 0.90 against 0.53 and 0.60 against 0.20 at 3,000: always higher and always beyond 2 sd, so verdicts cost standing in ties more in a shocked town.

**R4, trust.** Not met and, in the mean, not meetable as built. Holders against others of an event about the struck firm: +101 (gb-eng, one firm), +52 and +24 (other firms), +191 and +111 (3,000), and several at -100 to -70, none reaching 200 bps and none with more than one seed. A walk-out bears on trust in the employer by the sign of each person's own view of striking, and strike views are symmetric around 50 (own 50 +- 17), so the mean over holders is near zero by construction (holders of shop-16's walk-out: -4 bps). The police: holders about -550 to -820 against others, in shocked and unshocked arms alike (a removal's event, same in both).

**The said/thought gap and pluralistic ignorance.** Gap between what people think and say: 4.9 at the start and 4.1 to 4.2 at the end of the year, the same in both arms (differences 0.0 to 0.1). Pluralistic ignorance sits only where a profile's figure is off the middle (`join_union`: 12.4% at the start to 7.5% shocked, 7.9% unshocked in gb-eng; 22.8% to 17.1% against 17.0% in ke-nakuru): it falls the same in both arms. For `strike` it is 0 in both from the start (everyone starts at 50), so there was none for a published ballot count to break; published counts occurred in both arms (3 results unshocked, 6 shocked in gb-eng) and left `strike` approves at 50.0. What the town takes others to approve against what people think: `join_union` gap 1.6 against 0.9 (gb-eng, beyond 2 sd) and 1.0 against 0.8: a little more disagreement, not less.

**Memory.** Events held by people: 79% (gb-eng), 76% (au-vic), 79% and 66% (3,000), the same in both arms. A strike held: gb-eng 1,000 41 holdings a run (0 unshocked), gb-eng 3,000 361 (37), ke-nakuru 139 (23); au-vic 0. Came by seen/read/told: strikes are first seen only by those who struck (the members who stopped work, as built) and then told: in gb-eng 3,000 shocked, through two hands 502 against 416, through three 309 against 116 (the second beyond 2 sd); ke-nakuru: told 6,354 against 5,772, through two hands 1,924 against 1,515. Removals seen in ke-nakuru: 475 against 194 (beyond 2 sd, 4,745 holdings of a put-out against 3,638), because the shocked town had more people living near a removal, not more removals (warrants carried out do not differ). How far: seed 1, gb-eng: the first stoppage, day 126; 1 holder at day 150, 30 at 210, 86 at 270, 164 at 330, 189 at 364 (through three hands: 12, 42, 92, 102 of all the slots held).

**Does culture change the town's course?** No. Dial on against off, gb-eng 1,000, five seeds: shocked 0 of 57 standing measures beyond 3 standard errors, unshocked 0 of 57. The union's share of members at the year's end: 7.96 against 7.60 shocked (z -1.8), 7.90 against 7.88 unshocked; departures 154.4 against 149.2 (z -1.3) shocked, 140.6 against 138.2 unshocked. Stoppages 1.4 against 1.2 and strike ballots 3.6 against 3.0 (dial off against on; inside the noise). Shocked against unshocked, on or off, moves 28 to 34 measures, and the same ones. The union's share does not change with the shock in any town (z between -1.1 and +2.1: au-vic `firm_last_pct` 0.96 to 1.46, 2.1, one line in 57); people leaving: +18 (gb-eng, z 7.5), +44 (gb 3,000, 7.5), +210 (ke-nakuru 3,000, 14.5), au-vic +4 (1.0).

**Tipping events:** 0 in every 1,000-person run, shocked or not; decisions recorded are 100 to 213 a run, spread over four conducts and groups, so a window of 8 decisions in one group is rare. Not readable at 3,000 (lean log).

**Verdict (by the criteria fixed before the runs): no for the mean of what people take others to do and approve; partly for what people say and for standing.** In the 1,000-person arm, where the criteria can be applied (five seeds, two profiles): R1, R2 and R4 are not met in either profile; R3 is met for verdicts (gb-eng which bites, au-vic which does not). Where something pushed, what responded was **talk and standing** (more verdicts, more people told "right", more cooled ties), and the town's course did not change with culture. The picture of what others do and approve did not move by a point. Plainly: culture responds to a shock by talking more, not by changing minds.

**Two stories** (gb-eng, 1,000 people, seed 1, rerun for the log). c0861, a union member who voted yes in the ballot ("I say voting for action is right", and also "I say joining the union is wrong": a gap between what is said and the vote cast), was the only member to stop work at shop-16 on day 126. It told c0858 at 9 in 10, c0132, c0929, c0860, c0463 and others; c0858 (laid off by shop-17) told c0230 at 7 in 10 through one hand, c0230 told c0678 at 4 in 10 through two hands, c0678 told c0679 at 3 in 10 through three hands, where it stops. Each of them also told its own acts alongside. c0132 told c0146, who says voting for action is wrong, and c0146 told c0802, who joined the union at a new job and says joining is plainly wrong. Nobody who held it changed what they take others to do (the holders' `strike` does is 85.5 against 85.0 for the rest): the event was passed along four hands and moved no number. Second (3,000 people, ke-nakuru): seven to eight stoppages a year against two; 135 holders of a remembered strike a run, and 4,745 holdings of a removal.

**Faults and oddities, described and not fixed.** (1) **A route that fires and changes nothing: a walk-out held, told and remembered by hundreds changes no one's `does` or `approves` for `strike`.** By design a walk-out taken part in is not a sighting of the conduct (docs/behaviour/culture.md, town memory); the stoppers hold it as their own and hearers get it as a "talk of the town" item that feeds only memory and trust. So the one conduct the shock touches most (`strike`) has no route from the event to the picture. Evidence: 189 holders of a stoppage in seed 1, holders' `strike` does/approves 85.5/50.1 against 85.0/50.0. (2) **R4 cannot register in the mean** (above): the bystander effect is signed by each person's own view, symmetric around 50, so a mean is near zero; the measure reports a mean only, not how many moved up or down. (3) `join_union` `does` falls in the shocked town and keeps falling at year end: the likely route is fewer new jobs, so fewer occasions to join, not a norm; the decisions are not shown by cause here. (4) `put_out` holdings differ between arms by a lot (gb-eng 257 against 93) with the same number of warrants: the holdings follow who is in which building, not events, and one seed carries most of it (sd of pairs 258). (5) The measure `trust_moved` has fewer than three "others" in most firms, so a party row is one seed. (6) The strike holders in the unshocked arm are 0 to a few dozen, so R2's calm comparison is against zero. None changes the verdict.

**Not verified:** a shock that removes people (removals; none can be provoked); the 3,000 tipping events; the 3,000 verdict with five seeds; whether the `join_union` drift is the norm or the job market (the dial-off arm holds no norms to tell); the dial-off arm of the 3,000-person town and of au-vic.

**Revisit if** a route from a walk-out seen to the picture of `strike` is wanted (the owner's call; it is a design question, not a size), a removal can be provoked and the proof is run on it, or the bystander effect is read by direction as well as in the mean.


## 2026-10-14 · Culture, the join, the trust measure and a second proof (one bounded pass, then stop; no model, no pilot)

The first proof (above) found a design gap, not a size: a public event a person saw, heard of or remembers changed nothing in their picture of what others do or approve (memory, step 5, and norms, steps 1 to 4, were built side by side and never joined), and one measure, trust among those who remember, could not pass by construction. The owner asked for one bounded pass, in order, then to stop either way: join them; fix that measure; rerun the same proof once. Three commits, one each.

**1. The join** (`Culture.sawEvent`, `EVENT_CONDUCTS` in `townmemory.ts`). A public event that is an instance of a typed conduct, **when it first becomes mine** (seen, read or told, and kept: the moment it first bears on trust), is one sighting of that conduct by the existing rule (`moveDoes`) at the existing weight of the route (here 1, tie 1, close tie 2) **times how strongly the event is held**, so a retold event counts for less exactly as its strength already says (`pass_bps` of the teller's a hand, 80% for what I hold wrong, let go past three hands). The teller's said view (their `says` of the conduct, voiced only when not the middle step, as everywhere in culture talk) rides on the "Talk of the town" phrase ("Of that, I say it is wrong.") and is one hearing of approval at the same weight. **No size is new**: nothing was added to `CultureParams`. Mapping: a removal under a warrant is a sighting of `apply_possession` and `stay_past_notice` (seen: unchanged, already so; told: new); a walk-out is a sighting of `strike` (told: new; for those who took part it is still their own act, not a sighting). The other four of the six kinds (`ruling`, `law`, `vote`, `founded`) show no conduct of the list; taking-in, a tribunal application or answer and a complaint are conducts of the list but no public event kind carries them, so they are not joined (a new kind would be a change to the closed list); a founding cannot be told to be a union's from its purpose statement. Nobody has a god's view: only an event seen, read or told reaches the picture, `sawEvent` refuses any other route, an event counts once however often it is told (`again` and `dropped` count nothing); cases in `participants/test/culture-events.test.ts` and `orchestrator/test/no-god-view.test.ts`. Dial off byte-identical to main (`culture-dial`, living, reading, twin-draws; generator and goldens untouched). Basis: Cialdini, Reno and Kallgren 1990; Bicchieri 2006; Tversky and Kahneman 1973 (to confirm); in `docs/research/references.md`. **Revisit if** an event kind for a taking-in, an application, a complaint or a joining is wanted (then it is the six kinds that change), or if the weight of a retold event should not be its strength.

**The 85 question, answered.** A person starts at 85 "done" for `strike` because the conduct is "votes yes in a ballot for action" and its starting `does` is the conduct's own rate in this world: `strike_vote_yes_bps`, the chance a member who votes votes yes, **8,500, a placeholder** in the code and in `docs/behaviour/unions.md` ("placeholders: 70%, 85%. Protected action ballots usually pass"); no profile sets it. So the mapping from the draw to the conduct is faithful; what is off is the name (the picture held under `strike` is the voting, not the walking out) and that 85 has no source. Not plainly a mapping mistake, so not changed (it would move every calibrated ballot and the goldens). **Revisit if** the owner wants a sourced figure for a ballot's yes share (union-ballot results are published in several countries), or `strike` split into the vote and the walk-out.

**2. The measure.** Trust among rememberers read the signed mean of movement, which cancels by construction since each person's bearing takes the sign of their own view and views are spread round the middle. Added (`trustMovement`, `trustDirection`): each person's movement multiplied by the direction their own view gives (toward the party or away), as a mean and a share, for holders against others, among those with a view. The existing fields and every other measure and criterion are unchanged; the helper `trustDirection` is also what `bearOnTrust` reads, so measure and mechanism cannot part. Test: `orchestrator/test/culture-measures.test.ts`.

**3. The second proof.** Same design, seeds, shock (`goods` demand `factor_bps` 300 from day 0, friction x3, opening caseload, initiative 10,000), profiles, measures and criteria, the first proof's STATUS copied verbatim into `runs/culture-5/STATUS` (with a note of the one added reading of R4) before any run. 42 runs in two lanes through `scripts/slots.ts`; each log read once by `scripts/culture-proof.ts` and deleted; `scripts/culture-proof-sum.ts` (the directional R4 lines added) and `oikos diff` read the rest. Outputs in `runs/culture-5/` (outside git). Disk: 112 GB free at the start, never under 60 GB (others on the machine), 84 GB at the end; my own logs and measure dirs deleted (8.7 GB). Nothing was changed after seeing results.

*The town:* identical bites (ke-nakuru 48.7 against 9.3 events, was 46.0), identical standing differences (gb-eng, au-vic, 3,000 gb-eng: the diffs against the first proof's are byte-for-byte equal; ke-nakuru differs slightly).

*R1:* not met in any town. `strike` does at day 364, shocked minus unshocked: -0.0 (gb-eng), 0.0 (au-vic), +0.1 and +0.1 (3,000; beyond 2 sd, but a tenth of a point); approves 0.0 to 0.1; `join_union` drift unchanged (-0.6, -0.4, -0.2, -0.3), `take_from_employer` 0.0. 2 points needed.
*R2:* not met. Holders of a remembered strike against others, `strike` does: **+1.6 (gb-eng, 2 seeds with holders), +1.2 (gb 3,000), +1.8 (ke-nakuru)** against +0.6, +0.3, +0.7 before; approves +0.7, +0.5, +1.2 (before +0.8, +0.3, +1.1). The join works, in the right direction, and two to four times as large; it is under 2 points, `approves` hardly moves (a view is voiced only when not the middle step), and in ke-nakuru the calm arm's few holders differ more (+4.0).
*R3:* identical to the first proof and met for verdicts in both profiles (gb-eng 102 against 48, au-vic 132 against 74); people told right 51 against 24, 61 against 37; ties cooled 0.84 against 0.30, 0.66 against 0.38.
*R4:* the signed mean as before. In the direction the event gives: gb-eng police +181 (4 seeds, sd 224), shop rows 8, 65, 26 (one seed each); gb 3,000 -56 to +56; ke-nakuru police -92, shop rows -181 to +216 one seed each, the calm arm -433 to +148. None above 200 with more than one seed and no sign that holds. **Not met.**
*Course:* dial on against off, gb-eng 1,000, five seeds: **0 of 57 beyond 3 standard errors in both arms, the same differences as the first proof** (union share 7.96 against 7.60 shocked; departures 154.4 against 149.2). Culture does not change the town's course. *Tipping:* none (100 to 213 decisions a run; not readable at 3,000).

**Verdict: partly.** What people say and the standing it costs respond to a shock (R3), as in the first proof. The picture of what others do now responds in the people who hold the event, and not in the town; R1, R2 and R4 are not met; culture does not change the town's course. Not softened.

**Why the town's mean cannot reach 2 points by this route (arithmetic, not a fault).** A first told walk-out moves an 85 up by at most about 3 points (5 from a close tie), later ones by less as the weight held fills the window of 20; only 5 to 18% of a town hold the event (about 180 of 1,000, 355 of 3,000 in gb-eng, 137 of 3,000 in ke-nakuru); and the teller's view travels only when not the middle step (28% voice a view of `strike`). A town mean of +2 would need holders to move 11 to 40 points. Larger needs a larger event (more strikes, more of the town in them), a different weight for hearsay, or a different question.

**Story** (gb-eng, 1,000 people, seed 1, rerun for the log). The one member to stop work at shop-16 (day 126) told c0929 on day 165 at 9 in 10, saying striking is right; c0929's picture of what people do went from 85 to 90 and of what they approve from 50 to 55. The same walk-out reached c0146 on day 163 at 7 in 10 through one hand from someone who says it is wrong: c0146's `does` went 85 to 86 and `approves` 50 to 45. 182 people held it by year's end (2 first hand, 13, 51 and 116 through one, two and three hands); the further it travelled, the smaller the move. In the first proof the same walk-out moved nobody.

**Faults and oddities, described and not fixed.** (1) **The log cannot see small moves:** a record section is written again only when a figure has moved by 2 points (`norms`) or 100 bps (`trust`), so a person's later sightings and every bystander move on trust are invisible until they add up; the bystander effect itself is about 10 bps an event (`good_bps` 300 x `heard_bps` 50% x a bearing near 0.08), under the grain and far under R4's 200 bps. The `bystander_bps` size is a placeholder and the owner's; R4 as written would need either a much larger one or a record that writes trust finer. (2) An event's key is (kind, who it was about, day): two removals by the police the same day, or two walk-outs at the same employer the same day, are one event. (3) The ke-nakuru calm arm shows large holder-against-other differences (`strike` does +4.0, says +11.4) from 23 holders a run, mostly the people who struck themselves; a measured comparison needs more holders than the calm arm has. (4) `join_union` `does` and `approves` still drift down in the shocked gb-eng town (-0.6, -0.7) as in the first proof; the likely cause (fewer new jobs, fewer occasions to join) is still untested because the dial-off arm records no norms. (5) The unit `strike` is the voting, not the walking out (above).

**Not verified:** the join in a town with many more strikes; a removal-heavy shock (none can be provoked); the 3,000-person arm at five seeds; the dial-off 3,000 and au-vic arms; whether a stronger reading of retold events (not the strength) would be more realistic.

**Revisit if** the owner wants the picture to respond at the scale of the town: the levers are a larger event (the shock or the share who strike), the weight of a retold event, or splitting `strike` into the vote and the walk-out; and R4 needs a size or a record decision first.

## 2026-10-14 · Reading: the gate, run for real (step 5; the gate fails; steps 6 and 7 not built)

**What was done.** The model reader (`participants/src/llm/reader-model.ts`: an analyst's prompt in two wordings, a closed answer object read exactly or not at all, every call recorded whole to a JSONL file as training data for a reader of our own), the gate's runner for models (`scripts/reading-gate.ts`: spend tracked from Claude Code's own cost records, the run stops before the budget, replay of a recorded sitting at no cost), and seats' own words drawn from past pilots' logs for the author's-family check (`scripts/reading-family-papers.ts`; the logs read only). The gate was then run with Haiku 5.5 as the reader (lowest effort, extended thinking off), `gpt-6-luna` (answered on the first try) as a second reader of the other family, and Sonnet 5.5 as the second reader on the half of the pairs the budget allowed. All readings, the run's records and the reports are in `runs/reading-gate-2026-10-14/` on the run server (never deleted). **Thresholds, pairs, prompt and effect sizes were not changed after any result.** 803 calls recorded, 18.17 USD as Claude Code reckons it (Haiku 5.5 15.27 over 520 calls including 4 smoke calls at default effort; Sonnet 5.5 2.62 over 80 good calls; luna 193 calls on the Codex plan, not metered in dollars) of the 20 allowed.

**Result against the frozen thresholds (Haiku 5.5 reader, all 40 pairs; two-readers against luna on all 40, and against Sonnet 5.5 on 20).** Repeat FAIL (same 46.1%, within a step 50.8%; needs 80 and 97). Pairs FAIL (right 5 of 40; needs 36). Length FAIL (same 33.8%, largest mean move 0.66 step). Politeness alone FAIL (unmoved in 4 of 40, respect within bounds in 7). Names and sums PASS (80 of 80). Rewording FAIL (within a step 52.5%, same 45.6%). Two readers FAIL (Haiku and luna: same 42.2%, within a step 49.0%, lowest kappa 0.11, both right on 4 of 40; Haiku and Sonnet on the 20 pairs at even places: same 45.6%, within a step 50.8%, lowest kappa 0.46, both right on 4 of 20). Author's family PASS at the limit (largest own-family lift 0.25; needs at most 0.25), on 16 papers. Quoted phrases FAIL (2,310 of 2,605 lines, 88.7%; needs 95). Readable FAIL (169 of 704 askings unread, 24%; needs 5%; declined 1, by Haiku). Cost FAIL (0.0212 a call over the whole sitting with luna costed at 0; Haiku alone 0.029, Sonnet alone 0.033; needs 0.02). A code town with the dial on and the extreme readers are no model's: pending, as before. **Respect, reason and answers fail, so the slice does not go ahead, as 13f says. Steps 6 and 7 were not built.**

**Why: the likeliest reason, with evidence.** One failure feeds all the rest. The harness counts a reading whose phrases are not valid quotes as unread (13b: "a reading whose phrases are not is unread"), and an unread reading is a miss in every other check. 256 of the Haiku 5.5 phrase lines were longer than the twelve words the prompt allows (19 more were not in the paper); the same on 13% of Haiku 5.5's lines that were not 0, 9.5% of Sonnet 5.5's and 2.6% of luna's. With extended thinking off and the lowest effort, the reader copies a whole clause where it is asked to count to twelve. **A post hoc description, not a verdict** (`runs/reading-gate-2026-10-14/analysis/numbers-only.ts`: the same recorded readings, the same harness, the same thresholds, with a bad phrase let through so the numbers are judged alone; no call): repeat PASS (88.3%, 99.0%), rewording PASS (98.2%, 82.4%), names and sums PASS, quoted phrases and readable PASS by construction; pairs FAIL (right 27 of 40, other lines within a step in 35), length FAIL (same 78.5%, largest move 0.55 step), politeness FAIL (unmoved in 23 of 40; respect within bounds in 39), two readers FAIL (Haiku and luna: same 81.9%, within a step 96.8%, lowest kappa 0.46, both right on 19 of 40; Haiku and Sonnet on 20 pairs: 84.7%, 98.1%, 0.53, 11 of 20), author's family FAIL (0.43). So the phrase rule explains the repeat, the rewording and the collapse of the pairs, but not all of it: the numbers on their own still do not part the pairs, are moved by length and by pleasantries, and the two readers agree to within a step but not enough on which side. This is a statement about what the readings are, not a licence to pass them.

**Author's family.** On the papers seats wrote in their own words, Haiku 5.5 read the Claude-family seats' papers lower than luna did (respect -0.13, reason -0.25), so no favour; the larger gap is luna reading the gpt-family seats' papers higher than Haiku did (respect +0.43, reason +0.43, on 7 papers; non-zero on one or two). Low power: see the next paragraph.

**Faults and oddities, described and not fixed.** (1) **Past pilots hold almost no worded decision by a seat.** A decision's `reason` in the logs is a code module's template; the only prose seats wrote is each draft's `proposal` (instructions to an office: "Set up a payment of..."), and these read as respect 0 and reason 0 to 1 almost everywhere. So the author's-family check ran on instructions, not on papers written to a person, and had little to measure; a real answer needs worded decisions from a pilot of each family with the dial on. (2) **The gate's price is not the spec's.** 13f expected about 440 calls a reader at 0.02 USD or less; Claude Code reckons 0.03 to 0.07 a call (default effort 0.068, lowest effort and thinking off 0.029 for Haiku 5.5, 0.033 for Sonnet 5.5), and a full gate is about 700 calls for the reader and its second, so about 25 USD. The second reader's full 80 texts did not fit; it read half. (3) **My own mistake, found by the gate's stop rule:** the first sitting set `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0` for both Claude models, and Sonnet 5.5 refuses it (400 on every call, six in a row, no cost, no reading); the runner stopped itself, and the setting is now Haiku 5.5's only. (4) The runner's "other reader" for the family check is new (`runGate({ other })`): a second reader of the reader's own family cannot test a family's favour. (5) The twelve smoke-test calls (four at default effort, four at the lowest effort with thinking on, four at the lowest with thinking off) are in the same file, as readings of the first pair; the gate's replay leaves them out by time.

**Not verified:** a prompt that holds the twelve-word rule (the gate does not allow changing it; this is the owner's call); the same gate for Sonnet 5.5 as the reader; any Haiku reading with extended thinking on.

**Options for the owner** (not taken): (a) a reader-side rule that a phrase longer than twelve words is cut to its first twelve (still an exact quote), which would let the numbers be judged, and a new gate on a new prompt version, about 25 USD at today's prices, with Sonnet 5.5 as the reader; (b) accept that no external model reads these papers finely enough, and go to a reader of our own trained on these 700 readings and more, with the extreme-reader mocks (step 7) first; (c) give up reading for the first pilots. The numbers-only run favours (a) only for repeat and rewording; the pairs and the pleasantries control are failures of the reader, not of the rule.

**Revisit if** a reader passes the gate on a new prompt version; or the owner rules on the phrase rule.

## 2026-10-14 · The translator's third round, step 0: prompt 0.9.5, form-by-form release, the tools (no model called, no GPU)

**What was asked.** Step 0 of `docs/design/translator-round-3.md` (the plan the owner approved): the prompt written, `line` taught, the founding request naming a place, the per-form release list in the adapter, `--max-pieces`, generator kinds, the forms inventory per profile with token lengths, seen cases `r95-*`. Done in four commits on `tr3-step0`; the fast tier and what changed pass; the full suite was not run (the merge's).

**The owner's ruling of 2026-10-14, recorded.** *A form is handed to our model as soon as it passes its own per-form mark (at least 8 real cases, 90% right, no wrong draft, and 90% of its generated tests), even while the model as a whole is under 90%.* The model's folder carries the list (`forms-released.json`, beside `forms-trained.json`; `scripts/forms-released.ts` makes it and refuses a form the model was not taught; `readerOf` reads it). A form taught and not released is recorded and not offered as one never taught is (`form_unseen`: the draft is on the route as `wrote`, the translator behind drafts for the world). A folder with no list is read as before (the forms taught), so `pod-small-r2-s1` and every existing arrangement behave as they did; the arrangement itself is not touched. Non-form kinds are released with the model as a whole, as the plan says.

**What was built, and where the plan was wrong about the code.**
- **Prompt 0.9.5, sentences and worked examples only.** A payment drawn on a line of the budget carries `line=<label>`, none where none is named, and a line is not an account; `hours=` on an agreement only where the request states them (a length of time, "40 hours"); a notice of something held again and again is one statement with `practice=` and `on=`, an offer anyone may take up one statement with `offer=`, never an agreement. `line` is out of `CODE_ARGS` (contracts/calls.md and contracts/README.md say so; under the blanket approval of 2026-10-11; no schema change; no example a trained model learned names a line). Ten seen cases `r95-*`, each ruling both ways. **Plan wrong:** it had the practice and the offer written in seconds and smallest units, which is a calculation (the translator never calculates) and a currency in the rule. The prompt says the request's own words ("14 days", "90 minutes", "a month", "$20"); the translator's resolver reads them as a length of time and an amount are read, **for a translator's draft only** (`resolve(..., { written: true })`: whole seconds and a code participant's own data pass untouched). The Rust resolver is not changed and has no case in the shared tables for it: it is not on the translator's path.
- **Founding names a cell, not a lot.** The gathering's request reads "..., a practice held at <space>, on <cell>: ..." (`group.founded` 0.2.1, optional parameter `place_on`, the cell the home stands on, from `SiteStructure.at`; empty where not known, and the request is then as it was). **Plan wrong:** it said a lot; the citizen knows the building's corner cell and `on=` takes either. The module's own acceptance of the draft is unchanged (it ignores where the notice is put up). The citizen's version string was not moved (the parameter is new, optional and passed only where known); the entity's record carries the new parameter, so a founding world's state hash moves for that entity.
- **`line` in `ARGS` would have broken any slot-by-slot model's decoding** (a slot per allowed argument, in the contract's order): the decoder now uses the model's own `grammar` (config.json) where it has one. The deployed model writes steps (no `decoding` in its config), so it was never at risk; an export from now on has the new slot.
- **Generator kinds** (`lateKinds`, tags `line_payment`, `report_amounts`, `split_payment`, `hours_term`, `practice_notice`, `offer_notice`; options on `translator-data`; the default recipes' data for any seed is unchanged, tested). The `needs_calculation` refusals that state no share are made from the split programs (an extra brief only where there are such programs). **Plan wrong or silent:** `statement.practice` and `statement.offer` are in `JSON_OUT_OF_SCOPE` and the export cannot locate the scalars of non-flat data, so the trained model's export cannot encode the practice and offer kinds. They are made, and useful to the prompt-driven translators' evaluation; they teach the trained model nothing until `needed` and `encode` take them (a day's work, step 3's to decide). The plan's part "from code participants' calls" cannot give the 29 new forms either: on lv-06's own log (read only, counted) the gold from logs has one form call in 7,530 programs and none of a new form; code writes papers as statements with data. They are covered by `--world-forms` alone.
- **`--max-pieces`** (640, 1024 or 2048; `py/limits.py`) on the trainer: with an encoder a row of more pieces than this is dropped from training, so the long reader needs it with `--max-tokens 2048`.
- **The forms inventory** (`scripts/forms-inventory.ts`; `runs/translator-round-3-2026-10-14/forms-inventory.{json,txt}`): nine profiles, each seat's forms as the translator shows them, the model's own tokens, in three line-ups (the seat alone; the pilots' line-up; every office seated). **No list is over 2,048 anywhere** (the most 1,596, every office seated). Over 1,024: a letting office (26 forms, 1,455 to 1,460, in every profile), a shop's and a factory's manager (19 forms, 1,054 to 1,095), the tribunal's member and registrar in the pilots' line-up in four profiles (1,025), and every town office when all are seated (1,552 to 1,596).

**Not done.** Step 1 onwards; nothing was scored. `translator/eval/forms-shown.ts` does not yet read the release list (step 5). The held-out file was never opened; the repository's own check that no seen case, prompt or doc shares a run of five words with it passes (two seen cases of mine did, by their id only, and were reworded without reading it).

**Revisit if** the owner wants practice and offer in the trained model (then `needed` and `encode` take nested data and the closed values `join`, `dues` and `taker`); a pilot seat writes `line=` for a line the profile's budget does not have (the translator is not told the lines, it copies); a seat's list grows over the reader (then the inventory is run again: it is cheap); or the Rust resolver is put on the translator's path (then it needs the same reading of a practice's and an offer's words).
