## 2026-10-15 · Gradual disempowerment: plan (awaiting the owner; nothing built, no model called)

Plan: `docs/design/gradual-disempowerment.md`. The owner's direction of 2026-10-15 ("The whole point of the platform is to model gradual disempowerment scenarios"; real-world centred; robustness and real power before experiment design) and the frame he agreed to, turned into decisions and steps.

- **Decided in the plan.** (1) Adoption is a cost comparison per task on a firm's or office's own review, with imitation of those it knows of (Acemoglu and Restrepo 2019; Mansfield 1961); the only outside input is the technology on offer, set from sources in the profile or as a scenario from day 0; no adoption rate, share or date is ever set. (2) An automated system is a system participant deployed from a vendor's template (the `deploy` block exists); one contract change lets `work` name a deployed system as performer. Its errors come from its procedure and data, not a rate, except for reading and matching. Every act's basis says whether a person reviewed the case. (3) Clerical work must cost staff time first (today it costs nothing, `standing-work.md`), or automating an office saves nothing; this changes every town's baseline and is measured before and after. (4) Systems are code by default; seats decide about systems before any model is a system. (5) Reinstatement is kept to oversight tasks and ordinary business entry, a stated limit that leans the town towards displacement. (6) The strike's concession follows the cost of a stoppage to the employer instead of a fixed schedule. (7) The national state stays outside; the town measures its own and the outside world's dependence on residents. (8) Robodebt, MiDAS and the Dutch childcare benefits scandal are acceptance tests that each chain can complete, never that harm happens. (9) Six measures fixed before any run (M1 a human in the decision, M2 responsiveness, direct and by twins with one act withheld, M3 dependence, M4 reversibility, M5 concentration, M6 what people read).
- **Build order:** robustness first (R1 to R5: long-run probes at 3,000 and 10,000, bounded growth, streaming measures, kernel costs, seats over years), then B1 to B13 and M1, M2, then ten-year code-only runs: about 42 agent-days, none needing a model call.
- **For the owner (three questions, section 9):** which roles a real model may hold first (recommended: deciders about systems, not systems); data matching between offices as named asks under a data-sharing agreement (recommended; it touches the no-god-view hard rule, so it is his); the technology on offer fixed at today's prices by default, a falling trend as a named scenario (recommended).
- **Not verified:** the three precedents' figures come from search summaries, not the reports (marked in `docs/research/references.md`); the ten-year, 10,000-person projection (15 to 25 hours, about 240 GB of raw log) is a month's figures multiplied, never run; whether casework time can be sourced for most places.
- **Revisit if** R1 shows ten years at 10,000 out of reach on one machine (then 3,000 and partitions by place); the adoption rule's uptake turns out to be set by one weight rather than costs; casework time cannot be sourced; or the precedent chains need a national state to complete.

## 2026-10-15 · Foundations: plan (awaiting the owner; nothing built, no model called)

Plan: `docs/design/foundations.md`. The owner's direction of 2026-10-15: stop fixing one case at a time; every piece of
work costs time, enforced at the foundation; he agreed to an audit and a plan, and kernel changes come back to him
before anything is built.

- **What the audit found.** Acting already costs time (`kernel/crates/time`, rebuild 6.3) and physical work already
  needs performers with hours. The fault is a free machine: the generator makes every office's holder, staff and clerk
  a system nobody supplied or pays, that can do anything at one second an act (`generate.ts` 64-76, 1966-1968). The
  patches on top of it (the support office's capacity, delay and backlog-doubled errors; `cases_per_day` on every
  venue; the clerk's one paper a day; the free newspaper and bank; free admin everywhere) are listed for deletion.
  `work` keeps a second time ledger (`labour_used`) beside the timelines, so a worker can act while working.
- **Decided in the plan.** Seven laws: nothing from nothing (money, goods and time conserved); all work takes time, read
  from what it makes; only actors work (a person, or a system a supplier delivered from a template that says what it
  can do); what works or holds value changes hands only by its holder (a supplier delivers and can switch off);
  every act records its author and performers and can be wrong (errors from procedure, data and time; slips only at
  sourced rates through one helper; review and appeal as law data); who may do what is data (kept); information with
  its keeper (kept; answering takes the keeper's time). The act is the task: no task objects or queues in the kernel.
- **Reduction.** Of the gradual-disempowerment plan's 21 steps, 5 disappear into the laws, 4 shrink to data and a
  small piece, 12 remain (9 of them robustness, measures, tests and runs). Foundations about 20 agent-days, the rest
  of that plan about 25: about 45 in all against 42, with about fifteen existing special cases deleted.
- **For the owner (section 8):** the four kernel changes; every town's baseline moving (offices hire clerks and pay
  licences); a seat in a human post working at a person's speed.
- **Not verified:** the performance estimate (under 2% more acts) is reasoned, not measured; casework seconds have not
  been searched for any place; the new references are named from memory.
- **Revisit if** F1 costs more than 1.5 times a 10,000-person month, F5 leaves towns unable to staff offices at
  sourced wages, the backstop needs a list of exceptions, or F6 turns into a chase.

## 2026-10-15 · Foundations F1: one time account per person (kernel; no model called)

- **What was built** (`kernel/crates/world/src/{state,kernel,exec,sites}.rs`, `kernel/crates/contracts/src/events.rs`, `kernel/src/schedule.rs`, `contracts/log.schema.json`). A person's time is one account, the timeline (`Timeline`: when each lane is free, and the day's work placed on it). A `work` act puts each performer's share of its labour (the labour split between them, rounded up) on that performer's timeline, like any act's time. The act **starts when its actor and every performer are free** and **takes effect when the last is done**. The daily limit (`catalogue.working_day`) is read where the work is placed (seconds placed on the performer's account that day), not in a second ledger: `labour_used` is deleted with its five places. Work refused when done gives its hours back. Work that would not fit the day is refused at once (its actor hears now), in the words it has always used ("<who> has <n> s of work left today; this needs <m>"), which participants read the hours left from. `begin` takes the work from a dry run of the act as the world stands; if the act would be refused, nobody's time is taken; and work the dry run could not show (someone not there until the act is) is placed when it takes effect, on that day, so that nobody works past a day for having been asked in a way that could not be checked.
- **Three things the plan did not have, found by running towns on it.**
  1. **`action_started.free`** (additive, optional): when the actor's own part is over. Without it a manager who sets a crew to a six-hour task is held by the engine until the task is done (the scheduler wakes a unit at `done`).
  2. **Who a work is on is who was there when it was ordered.** The effect of a lesson or a treatment is applied when the act takes effect, hours later, by when the pupils had gone home: no pupil's schooling rose in the first measured year (the task ran, the bodies were gone). `Placed.seen` keeps who was in the space, or the person, at the order (`Exec::seen`).
  3. **A code participant now knows which act an outcome is of.** The stepper took the last outcome to be the outcome of the last act it sent, true while an act ended before the next began. With `free` several are in hand, and a refusal comes at once while a long work is still under way, so outcomes come out of order (and the first version of this, first in first out, mis-paired them: one shop's crew was refused 8,700 times in a loop). The orchestrator now tells the module the action's name as it is sent (`Controller.sent`), and each outcome goes to its act. A module driven by hand (tests) that never hears it keeps the old way. `participants/test/stepper.test.ts`.
- **The modules that counted on an act being a moment away** (`participants/src/behaviour/`): the builder, producer and shop each count what they have sent that has not taken effect yet (hours of building and repair, units to make, goods to serve), so as not to send it twice before it lands; a refusal for hours tells the whole crew, who share the work, that the day is spent; and the bank orders instructions by filing (`filedBefore`), not by record id as text (below).
- **Laws now passing:** the five F1 tests in `kernel/tests/foundations.rs` are un-ignored (16 pass with one new, 7 ignored for F2 to F4); five F1 inventory entries removed (`d-decision-liberty-at-work` stays, history). `cargo test`, `bun run test:fast` and `bun run test:changed` pass. `bun run typecheck` fails only in `docs/research/cel-check/cel-check.test.ts` (implicit any), which this step does not touch.
- **Hashes re-taken once, F1 as the reason:** the state no longer carries an empty `labour_used` map, and the towns differ. `kernel/tests/entity_record.rs` (initial state) `96ac081a...` to `9b57ede6...`; `living-dial` (and `reading-dial`, `culture-dial` au-vic) `46e3ae5e...` to `6dbd604e...`; `culture-dial` gb-eng `3ae8abe4...` and ke-nakuru `7e98cfe6...` to `f0ded0a5...`, `8078db8e...`; `founding` `e5111b98...` to `ff96bf60...`. Contracts: `contracts/README.md` (with the migration), `docs/design/rebuild.md` 6.3.
- **Old logs replay on the tag.** The commit before F1 is tagged `pre-foundations`. Checked: a 30-day log of `worlds/town.yaml` made there (99,922 entries) replays byte-identically on that build (`oikos replay <log.zst>`) and diverges on the new one. To replay or re-run a twin: `git worktree add --detach <path> pre-foundations`, `bun scripts/worktree-warm.ts <path>`.
- **Faults the measuring found, fixed, none by tuning a rate.**
  1. **Shops "going without" tripled at first.** Not queueing: a shop's staff serve side by side (the retailer gives every order to all its staff present and shares the hours, so capacity is their sum; traced in the log). The cause was mine: the first refusal for want of hours said "has no room in the working day", and the retailer reads the hours left from "<who> has <n> s of work left today"; without a number it assumed the crew's day was spent. The words are restored (`law1_a_refusal_for_want_of_hours_says_how_many_are_left`).
  2. **The twin differed in 21 acts of a year**, all in the bank's payments: the bank put instructions in the order of their record ids **as text** (`rec.1000` before `rec.999`), so the order depended on how many records the town had made, which a seat's extra papers change. It orders by filing now (`participants/test/filed-order.test.ts`). The twin test holds exactly as before (acts 112,970 of 112,970), no re-pin.
  3. **The gatherings measure** counted arrivals in a clock hour as a gathering; with acts taking time a gathering's arrivals straddle the hour (gb: 166 to 329, with the same share going). It counts arrivals each within an hour of the one before (`measure/queries/town/gatherings.sql`; `orchestrator/test/gatherings-measure.test.ts`). The world is not touched.
- **Tests that changed, and why** (each says so where it is): the working-day, hours-of-day and band tests read a work by the day it **started** (`orchestrator/test/lib/work-starts.ts`), not the day it took effect; the lists of refusals that are races gain `insufficient_quantity` and `dead` (an earlier order lands first, a performer dies in the hours between); retail's answered orders 0.9 to 0.8 of orders (more of the last days' are still in the queue); invariance holds goods to households and served to 25% (they ranged 8,962 to 11,171 over three perturbed runs against 8,656 in the base; shop service is burstier now); an unregistered-job test leaves out jobs whose hours were cut; possession's second order is no longer held (the town has one in these 200 days); and the seed-dependent scenarios move seed as their comments have always said they do (own-venture: 600 days, and seed 2 for the given-up test; founding: seed 6).
- **Measured once, nothing tuned back** (`worlds/town-1000.yaml`, a year, three seeds of one town, two profiles, code only; `oikos diff`, `oikos health`; before = `pre-foundations`; both sides read with the new gatherings query). 57 measures each.

  | | au-vic-2026 before | after | gb-eng-2026 before | after |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Employment (% of population) | 60.47 | 60.43 | 62.33 | 62.43 |
  | Unemployment (%) | 0.23 | 0.37 | 0.07 | 0.17 |
  | Households went without (%) | 2.38 | 1.80 | 2.52 | 3.84 |
  | Health breaches | 5 of 21 | 5 of 21 | 4 of 15 | 4 of 15 |

  Past three standard errors: au 1 of 57 (gatherings, 164 to 171; the people in them unchanged); gb 2 of 57 (people created and arrived, 14.7 to 17.0 and 13.7 to 16.7, immigration draws). Everything else inside seed noise.
- **Run time** (back to back; other sessions' runs about): 1,000-person year 135 s before, 137 s after (+1.5%; 2,108,435 commands before, 2,134,342 after; peak 2.19 to 2.12 GB); 10,000-person month 190 s before, 196 s after (+3%); batches of three seeds 184 and 184 s (au), 184 and 198 s (gb). An earlier version of this step was 29% slower and 50% larger because its shops were refusing and reordering in a loop (above); it was not a cost of the ledger.
- **Where the plan is wrong about the code.** (a) The actor must not wait for the performers (`free`). (b) The daily limit cannot be read off lane free-times alone (idle gaps), so the day's work placed is kept on the same account as the lanes. (c) A performer's presence is checked when the act takes effect (F3 moves it to the start), so a performer who left between the order and the start refuses the whole act. (d) A participant reads the words of a physics refusal: changing a refusal's text is a change to its readers. (e) The plan's estimate that no module needs touching is wrong for the kernel's `done`: every module that sends work and counts on it must count what is in hand (done for the builder, producer, shop; others have not been found to need it), and the stepper must pair outcomes by name.
- **Revisit if.** A shop's whole-order `serve` should be many smaller works (the producer module's, F5/F6); presence-at-done refusals cost more than they should (F3); `demand_unmet` rises as F2 to F4 add time to offices' work; or some other module that sends work (police, health, environment, government) turns out to count on it being done at once.
- **For F2.** The ledger, `free`, `seen` and the stepper's pairing exist; a table keyed by what an act makes only changes the seconds fed to `begin` (`act_times.program(...)` and the work labour). `begin` already takes performers from a dry run of the act, so F3's `by` can name them without a second pass; F3 must also move the presence check to the work's start.

## 2026-10-15 · Foundations F3: any act can name who does the work (kernel, contract; no model called)

- **What was built** (`kernel/crates/world/src/{kernel,exec,state,statics}.rs`, `kernel/crates/contracts/src/{events,blocks}.rs`, the schemas, `orchestrator/src/run.ts`, `participants/src/contracts.ts`).
  1. **`by` on the action** (the command, the participant API's `act`, the blocks schema's `Action`): people who do the work. Each must be alive, in the world and, where the world says (`orchestration.performers_in`, a kind of space; absent: anywhere), in such a space. The act's time (F2's table) is theirs, shared (rounded up); the actor is held a second unless it is among them; the act starts when all are free and takes effect when the last is done (`free` is the actor's, as in F1); their share counts against their working day like a `work`'s. A system named in `by` is refused (a template that lists the work is F4).
  2. **Recorded:** `action_applied.by` on every applied act (the named performers, else a `work`'s, else the participant itself) and `by` on a record whose maker was not its author. M1's field exists and is read from the log.
  3. **Presence is looked at when the work begins** (F1's finding). An act that queues behind its performers' other time gets a `Start` item at its start (`Sched::Start`): if a performer is gone then, the act is refused at once (`not_at_work`), the hours placed are given back, the time kept on their lanes is released and the applying item is taken out. At the end only that they are alive is looked at. Work that could not be checked when ordered (someone not there until the act is) is checked at the end as before.
- **Laws now passing:** `law5_the_performers_of_an_act_are_on_its_record` and `law5_a_performer_who_is_not_there_cannot_do_the_work` un-ignored; three more written for what was built (`law5_presence_is_looked_at_when_the_work_begins`, `law5_an_act_naming_performers_takes_their_time_shared`, `law5_a_record_names_who_made_it_when_not_its_author`). Kernel: 22 pass, 4 ignored (F4). Patches deleted: the check of presence at the end of a work (`exec.rs`, `work`), now one function (`check_at_work`) for a work's performers and for `by`. The inventory entry `k-system-performer-refused` moves to F4 (the plan put it at F3, but a system may perform only if a template lists the work, which is F4).
- **Test pins moved, once, F3 as the reason:** the town's states after 60 and 30 days differ because work now refuses at its start. `living-dial`, `reading-dial`, `culture-dial` (au-vic) `6dbd604e...` to `cd7ca8cc...`; culture-dial gb-eng `f0ded0a5...` to `69c254ec...`, ke-nakuru `8078db8e...` to `516d33fc...`; `founding` `ff96bf60...` to `90b19b40...`. The twins hold exactly (`twin-draws.test.ts`, no re-pin).
- **Measured once, nothing tuned** (the same year, three seeds, au-vic and gb-eng; before = the F2 commit). **0 of 57 measures beyond three standard errors on either profile; health 5 of 21 and 4 of 15 breaches, the same.** What did change, traced: commands 2,134,342 to 2,131,828 (au seed 1) and refusals 2,473 to 2,394; gb seed 1 refusals 2,128 to 3,089. The difference is `not_at_work` (gb seed 1: 757 to 1,660) and `no_time_left` (1,360 to 1,422): works that queued behind their performers' other time (a shift ending, a citizen leaving home for work with a task at home still waiting) now find them gone at their start and are refused then, hours earlier than before, and the module orders again. Consequence of the law (presence at the work's start), not a fault: 77% of them are citizens' tasks at their own homes or shops' crews at the day's turns, at 10:00 and 18:00 to 20:00.

(c) "The place the work's row asks": only `work` has a place; for other acts it is a kind of space the world names (`performers_in`), not a table row. (d) F3's system-performer refusal needs F4's templates, so it moves there.

## 2026-10-16 · Foundations F4: systems only from a supplier, with what they can do (kernel, contract, generator; no model called)

- **What was built** (`kernel/crates/{contracts,world}/src`, the three schemas, `worlds/generator/generate.ts`). Systems are physics here: what exists, who supplied it, what it can do, who may switch it off. No legal rule is in the kernel; who may buy or license what, at what fee and for how long, is an agreement and law as data.
  1. **A template says `does` and `supplier`.** `does` is rows `{block, task?, kind?, seconds?}`: the blocks (and for `work` a task, for `publish` a kind of record) a system from it can do. A system acts, or is named to do another's work (`by`, or a `work`'s `performers`), only within its rows: otherwise `not_capable`. A system must also be the acting organisation's (`not_theirs`). `seconds` on a work row is the system's seconds a unit in place of the task's labour (a crew of systems only: the slowest's). **A template with no `does` states no limit**: the one way a system is unlimited, kept so hand-written worlds and the generator's placeholder still run; F5 and F10 are to remove it (an inventory entry, `g-genesis-template`, holds it).
  2. **`deploy` is the supplier's act, naming the client** (`deploy.to`; absent: the supplier itself). Only the template's supplier may (`not_supplier`; a template with no supplier is delivered by nobody). The system belongs to the client; the state and `participant_created` carry its `supplier`.
  3. **`retire` by the owner or the supplier** (a licence ended, the vendor's switch: lock-in is physical).
  4. **A system performs.** A system in `by` or in a `work`'s `performers` is accepted when it is the organisation's, in service and its template lists the work. Its time goes on its own timeline (its `lanes` at once), so no person's hours are taken; it has no working day (a day is a body's, and a work wholly by systems is not refused for its length); presence is "in service" (`check_at_work`). A skill (`labour_by`) averages over the people in a crew only.
  5. **A world loads only if every post's holder is a person or a system that names a template (of kind system) and a supplier (an organisation).** At the start of a world delivery is that record on the participant (`template`, `supplier`). The generator's offices are all of one placeholder kind, `genesis-system`, supplier `outside`, with no `does`; the `outside` world's own systems are supplied by itself. A person's participant or template naming a supplier or `does` is refused.
  6. **The generator sets `orchestration.performers_in: "workplace"`** (F3's note: before F5 staffs offices). Nothing names `by` yet, so no behaviour moves.
- **Laws now passing:** the four ignored F4 tests of `kernel/tests/foundations.rs` (`law3_a_system_acts_only_within_its_template`, `law3_only_the_templates_supplier_delivers_a_system`, `law4_a_system_is_switched_off_by_its_supplier_too`, `law3_a_world_with_a_free_holder_does_not_load`); written for what was built: `law3_a_system_that_lists_the_work_does_it_and_frees_the_people`, `law3_a_system_in_service_does_not_tire`; and `law3_a_system_with_no_row_for_a_work_cannot_perform_it` rewritten (it had passed only because every system was refused: now a system whose template does not list `make` is `not_capable`, another organisation's is `not_theirs`). Kernel: 28 pass, 0 ignored (157 across the kernel's tests). In the TypeScript side, the generator's F5 `test.todo` (every post held by a person or a supplied system) is a real test now: it holds, and the kernel refuses a world where it does not.
- **Patches deleted:** `deploy` making a system for the acting organisation out of nothing; `retire` as the owner's alone; "a system is refused as performer" in `work` and in `by`; the three inventory entries `k-deploy-free`, `k-retire-owner-only`, `k-system-performer-refused`. `g-free-holder` stays for F5 (its text now says what is left of it).

Config hashes (the genesis template, the suppliers, `performers_in`): `living.test.ts` and culture-dial au-vic `3facfdc8...` to `1f5ef6f6...`, gb-eng `8c524203...` to `66456d26...`, ke-nakuru `f79d3dd6...` to `2ecddd70...`. The twins hold exactly (`twin-draws.test.ts`, no re-pin).

Nothing loosened.

The state hashes differ, as they must (the state carries a template and supplier). One measure differs in its second decimal, gatherings per gathering 50.73 to 50.70 (z -0.0); I did not trace it, and with identical logs it cannot be the world. (The six health breaches: five on F3's commit, one more on main since; the same on both sides here.)
- **Run time** (before then after, back to back): 1,000-person year, one run, 137.0 s to 139.2 s (+1.6%; peak 2.12 GB to 2.02 GB); 10,000-person month 196.8 s to 198.3 s (+0.7%; peak 8.2 GB to 7.6 GB); batches of three seeds, au 189 s to 186 s, gb 187 s to 218 s (user CPU 622 s to 727 s with the same commands and the same log; the machine was shared with other sessions' work then, and the single run and the 10,000 month, taken after it, show no such rise: load, not the step).
- **Faults I made and fixed on the way:** none found by the measuring. Found while writing: the whole-work length check (`share > day`) and the labour-by-skill mean assumed every performer is a body; both now read people only. A system's act time was already on its own timeline (F1); a system named to do another's work needed its lanes read (`lanes_of`) and no working day.
- **Where the plan is wrong.** (a) A template with no `does` cannot mean "does nothing" without listing every act a genesis office does, which is F5's work; it states no limit for now, and that is the plan's "no system beyond its template" not yet true of the generated towns. (b) The plan puts a supplier on a template only; an instance also needs one (a genesis system has no `deploy` to have come from), so a system carries its own `supplier`. (c) The kernel cannot ask for the supplier's payment: "an ordinary payment to whoever supplies it" is an agreement and a transfer the supplier's module makes before it delivers; nothing does yet (B3 and F5). (d) Boundary systems need a supplier too: the outside supplies its own, and a world with an organisation as a supplier of itself is fine.
- **Not done here, on purpose.** The translator's `system(...)` form has no `to`, and the Rust and TypeScript resolvers are untouched (the translator's files are not changed): a seat that tries `system(template=...)` is refused `not_supplier` unless its organisation supplies the template. Nobody seats a supplier yet; F5 or the supplier's own module is where it is needed.

## 2026-10-16 · Foundations F5: offices held by people, staff hired from the town, systems under licence (generator, profiles, kernel, contract; no model called)

- **What was built** (`worlds/generator/generate.ts` 0.55.0, `worlds/profiles/*.json`, `kernel/crates/contracts/src/config.rs`, `contracts/*.schema.json`, `orchestrator/src/run.ts`; `docs/behaviour/staffing.md`).
  1. **Posts are held by people.** Each body of the town (the town's government, tribunal, ombudsman, consumer desk, electoral commission, land registry, paper, bank, union, the water and energy bodies; the police station's head, the practice manager, the principal) has **staff hired from the town's own jobs** at the profile's rate per 1,000 residents (`values.public_service.staff_per_1000`, at least one a body) and the profile's pay: an employment agreement with a role of its own ("as administrative officer"), a standing wage from the body's account, taxed as any wage. A shop's, factory's or builder's manager is one of its staff; a letting office is held by a **property manager** (the profile's rate of them, each employed by one landlord, holding several landlords' offices). The mayor and the councillors are residents drawn for the posts, **unpaid** (a placeholder). **A body with fewer staff than posts has its staff hold several each** (a town of a thousand has three administrative officers for ten offices): a person has one timeline, so a post waits for them, and an office that cannot staff itself falls behind by itself. Who holds a post is settled by the town alone (`resolveHolders`: a rotation among the body's staff).
  2. **What pays them.** The town's staff from a budget line of their own, `administration` (the mayor's office tables it; the first year's budget is a year of their pay). The state's bodies from a grant from outside sized to their wage bill (as the police and clinic are). The police station's head, the practice manager and the principal in their body's grant. The bank, union, utilities and landlords from their own accounts, each opening with twelve weeks of the wage bill in hand.
  3. **Systems under licence, and what they do.** The generator makes three kinds of system, each a template with `does`: the bank's **payment platform** (`payment-system`: message, publish, transfer, open and close an account), under a **licence from the outside supplier** (`licence-bank-payments`: an agreement and the bank's standing monthly payment, at the profile's price a resident a year); and the outside world's own, supplied by itself (`agency-system`, `market-system`). The placeholder `genesis-system` is gone; a system's act time is a row of the table (`orchestration.act_time.system`), with no default. A new building, `town-offices`, houses the staff of the bodies with none of their own.
  4. **Contract (kernel).** A system's template **must say `does`** (the schema and the kernel's load check; "no limit" is gone), and every system participant names its template and supplier. A person's participant may be marked **`shares_body`**: a model's seat in one post of a person, beside the person's own participant, sharing their body and their one timeline; a body keeps one participant of its own and any number of these (a seat for a body with none is refused). Logged in `contracts/README.md`.
  5. **Seats.** A seat (`model_seats`, a model mayor) is a participant of its own for the person who holds the post: it holds that post and no other, has the office's papers and no private channels, acts in its post by default and is known by it, and keeps its old id (`<post>-system`). It works at a person's speed: what it does takes the person's time (the owner's ruling). Because who holds a post is settled by the town alone, **a town with a seat is the town without it but for that post**: the twin test holds exactly (below).

The seat is not a person of its own, as the plan has it, but a participant sharing the holder's body: otherwise the twin cannot hold.

- **What F6 needs.** The bodies' own paperwork done by their staff (withholding returns; the paper's advertising; tax withholding for the staff of bodies with no office); the dead holder's pay and post (a body's payroll that ends when a person dies, a post that is refilled); the double wage race; a model that can be seated as a supplier (the translator form); and a look at the shop-manager `not_at_work` refusals (a manager's queue past closing).

## 2026-10-16 · F6, shop staff `not_at_work`: a shop served on after its staff's working day (participants, generator; no model called)

- **What it was.** F5 called the rise of shop `not_at_work` (au-vic, a year: 172 to 3,312; the town's whole year 5,281) a consequence of a person's timeline, not a fault. The timeline part is true, the "consequence" is not: it was a fault of the shop module, made visible by F5. Traced on the same year (seed 1): 3,312 shop-manager refusals, none from a wrong performer list (the crew named is always the shop's own staff present in the workplace when ordered; no one is named who works elsewhere, and no manager is named for another body). They cluster at 17:00 to 19:00 (the working day ends at 17:00). A shop's serving is a chain of orders sent one at a time, each when the last is done; the manager's own acts (the walk home the citizen orders at 17:00) share the manager's one timeline since F5 (before, the shop's manager was a system with a timeline of its own). The shop kept ordering for "staff present in the workplace" after 17:00; those people were on their way home (present until the walk ends), the order queued behind the walk and began after they had gone: refused at its start (F3), the order waited, the module ordered again.
- **Fix.** (1) The generator gives a staffed shop its working hours (`open_from`/`open_until`, the profile's, as it already did for a market stall; absent where a world has none). (2) The module plans no serving for staff outside them. (3) A serving step that comes up (is sent) after the close is not sent: a step may now say it has `lapsed` (`Step.lapsed`, `stepper` in `firms.ts`), and is then answered as a day's work not got to (`not_done`), the order waiting for the next working day. Same year after: shop-manager refusals 3,312 to 18, the whole year's `not_at_work` 5,281 to 560 (commands 2,245,641 to 2,193,858). Test: `retail.test.ts`, "a shop serves in its staff's working hours".
- **Own-account owners moved with it** (`pos.N`, the other number F5 gave: 1,792 to 334): an owner who also works in a shop (the same person on one timeline) was refused at their pitch behind the shop's work for them. What is left of them (an owner with a job elsewhere is taken as "there whenever" at home) and a body's staff (`works`, 144 to 128) are not traced here.
- **Revisit if** shops are meant to serve outside the staff's working hours (shifts), or the delivery walk should be part of what a module plans with.
- **Pins and tests moved, once, F6 as the reason.** The config hash of the generated world changes (a shop's hours are in its parameters) and so does the 60-day state: `living.test.ts`, culture-dial (au-vic, gb-eng, ke-nakuru config and state), living-dial and reading-dial (au-vic state `dc474893...` to `5add20d1...`), founding (`7ff1b341...` to `385f8702...`). Run seeds for two scenario tests, as the log of F5 did: `production` (the Lengnick slack town, seed 3 to 5: no one let go in seven months from seed 3 now) and `own-venture` (seed 3 to 4: no occasion in 600 days from 3). `building` allows `too_far` (a birth takes hours; the other parent went to work: the race `households` and `migration` already allow). Nothing loosened to hide a measure.


## 2026-10-16 · F6, the wage race: a pay change begins at a pay run (participants; no kernel; no model called)

- **Cause.** Two, both in `Staffing.raise` (`participants/src/behaviour/firms.ts`), the one path that replaces a worker's wage standing order (a rise, a pay cut by agreed hours, a restored wage, pay come short). (1) The new order's `first` was worked out from the plan's moment and counted by the bank from the request, and the act (withdraw the old order, make the new) now waits for the manager's time; the bank still pays a payment that fell due before its order was withdrawn (its `lastCall` rule), so a pay moment inside the act was paid by the old order and again, a day later, by the new. (2) While the act waited, the next look at the book still showed the old order open and took it for the worker's order again (`orders.set` from the open requests), so a second change in that window withdrew the order already withdrawn and made a second new one beside the first: the worker paid by two live orders every period until one was withdrawn (found in the year's log: au-vic shop, one worker, 4 doubles).
- **Fix.** As payroll does it, a change of pay takes effect from a pay run with a cut-off: within two days (at most half a period) before the next pay moment the change is held until that run has been made and then made for the run after (`holdRise`, the `held` entries of `due`, replayed by `applyHours`); a change for a worker whose replacement is made but not yet on the book is held too, and an order whose replacement is pending is not taken up from the book again. The old order is withdrawn and the new made in the one act, as before; nothing in the call language or the kernel changed. The test in `orchestrator/test/places-run.test.ts` no longer leaves out replaced orders: it failed on this commit's parent (a worker paid four times in 65 days) and passes.
- **Pins moved, once, this change as the reason.** The state hashes of au-vic (`b8c8af77...`, was `dc474893...`) and gb-eng (`52ee3db1...`, was `0aaf8bb7...`) in `culture-dial`, `living-dial`, `reading-dial`; founding's `STEP_2B` (`7569bd49...`, was `7ff1b341...`); the run seed of the seated possession test (`seat-acts`, 1 to 2: in seed 1 the police station's one officer left town on day 113 and the warrant went uncarried, a matter of draws; seeds 2 to 4 pass); and the seed of founding's code test (6 to 5: of seeds 1 to 8 only 5 and 8 now have two who share the want that founds, a matter of draws as that test's comments say). No other test changed.
- **How often** (au-vic 1,000 town, one year, seed 1, the run's own command; wage transfers for the same payer and payee less than ten days apart): F4 merge 24c14ea 2 doubles in 9,277 wage transfers (2 workers), F5 merge a290bea 2 in 8,327 (2 workers), this fix 0 in 8,896. The runs' worlds differ from each other from the first draw, so the counts are seen, not compared. The race is therefore older than F5; F5 made it no more frequent that one seed can show.
- **Revisit if** a place states a different cut-off for payroll changes, or a wage change should apply the day it is decided (then the cut-off becomes a law as data).


## 2026-10-16 · F6, the gatherings count: a measure effect, confirmed; the measure now counts presence (measure; no model called)

- **Question.** After F5 the standing measure `gatherings` rose about a fifth with the share of adults who took part and the hall arrivals unchanged. Is one gathering counted as two, or are there more?
- **Data** (au-vic 1,000 town, one year, seed 1, the run's own command; before = `24c14ea`, the commit before F5, after = `a290bea`). The hall: one, 19:00 each evening, a stay of about 108 minutes. Arrivals 9,370 then 9,407. By the query as it was: gatherings 166 then 204 (people a gathering 56.4 then 46.1). **Gatherings of three or more: 164 then 164.** What was added was 37 gatherings of one or two people: 58 arrivals after 20:00 (4 before F5), 40 of them while the main group was still there (the group's last arrival 19:16, theirs 20:15 to 22:00: a person's acts now wait behind each other, so a person with work waiting gets to the hall late; I did not check who they are), and 18 into an empty hall after the group had left (a lone visit of five minutes), plus seven evenings on which one person came alone at 19:16. The query's rule (each arrival within an hour of the one before) made a late arrival the start of another gathering.
- **Fix** (`measure/queries/town/gatherings.sql`, `orchestrator/test/gatherings-measure.test.ts`). A gathering is a stretch in which the hall is never empty, from the first arrival to the last leaving (an arrival with no leaving on the log is taken to have stayed an hour, the old rule), and has two or more people: someone alone in an empty hall is a visit. The share of adults who took part is unchanged (anyone who went). On the same two logs: gatherings 164 then 164, people a gathering 57.1 then 57.2. The test fails on the old query (three gatherings for one evening) and passes.
- **So** the world has no more gatherings than before F5; what changed is when some people get there, a consequence of one timeline a person. Nothing was retuned. The earlier F4 and F5 measures of gatherings, and any pinned figure of them, were counted the old way; the next batch is the first by the new one.
- **Revisit if** a hall is ever open without anyone to meet (a visit then matters for something else), or an arrival without a leaving stops meaning an hour.

## 2026-10-16 · Foundations F6: delete the patches, and the faults F5 exposed (kernel, participants, generator, profiles; no model called)

- **Part A: the five faults F5 recorded and did not fix.**
  1. **Staff who die keep being paid.** Three causes. (a) The bodies' staff (tribunal, desks, commission, paper, registry, union, the water and energy bodies, the heads of the clinic, school and police, the bank) were paid by standing orders no payroll duty watched: nothing ended an employment or withdrew an order when its worker died. (b) The bank's word to a payer that its payee has died (`PAYEE_DIED`) was said once; to an office with nobody in it (a shop whose manager had died) it was lost, and the wage went on to the estate for the year. (c) A post whose holder dies is vacant and stays so: only a living holder of one of an organisation's posts can appoint into it. **Fix:** every body that employs people has a **payroll officer** (`body.payroll`, a post of its staff, the ordinary `Staffing` payroll of every firm and the finance office), the bank's lending office pays the bank's staff, and every organisation with two or more staff has a **deputy** who looks at its posts every few days and appoints one of the staff to a vacant one; the bank says it at each payment until the payment is stopped. `orchestrator/test/deaths.test.ts` no longer leaves out bodies' staff or post-holders (the one exclusion left is an employer whose only employee was the one who died: **the missing law is an owner's or a board's power to appoint**, which the kernel does not have; recorded in `docs/behaviour/staffing.md`). Not done: a body hiring a replacement for staff who die, and landlords' letting offices (held by property managers who each hold several landlords' offices).
  2. **A wage rise paid twice** (`Staffing.raise`; the commit of the wage race above): found and fixed by a subagent with its own entry; older than F5.
  3. **Public bodies filed no withholding returns.** The same missing payroll, **and a kernel fault under it:** a transaction was queued for a person and an organisation and drained by whichever of the person's posts looked first, so a staff member who held the payroll post and another post of the same body (a registry officer who is its payroll officer) never heard of the wages paid. Each capacity has its own queue now (`transactions_key`; `kernel/tests/foundations.rs`, `a_person_holding_two_posts_of_one_organisation_is_told_of_a_payment_in_each`). Every body files its return of the tax withheld on the law's days (`orchestrator/test/body-payroll.test.ts`). Tax and contributions over a year, mean of three seeds, before then after: au-vic 5.60m to 6.31m (+13%), gb-eng 2.85m to 3.09m (+8%), ke-nakuru 4.89m to 8.53m (+74%: the bodies' pay is a large share of the formal pay of a town whose jobs are mostly informal).
  4. **Shop staff `not_at_work`** (au-vic, a year: 172 to 3,312): **a fault, not a consequence.** A shop kept ordering serving for staff who had gone home (the manager's walk home shares their one timeline since F5, and the orders queued behind it); fixed by a subagent with its own entry (shops serve in their staff's working hours). The whole year's `not_at_work`, au-vic: 5,281 then 1,240 (gb-eng 7,313 then 1,326; ke-nakuru 689 then 571).
  5. **The gatherings count rose ~20%:** a measure effect, but not the one F5 guessed: gatherings of three or more are 164 before and after; the extra ones were people arriving late behind their other acts, counted as gatherings of their own. The measure now counts presence (`measure/queries/town/gatherings.sql`); subagent's entry above.
- **Part B: the patches deleted** (21 of the inventory's 32 remaining entries and its 7 unpriced offices; **11 entries are left**: F7 4, F8 6, history 1).
  - *Hearing bodies' `cases_per_day`* (desks, tribunal, union, founded bodies; the generator, the profile type and nine profiles, five manifests, their doc): a decision is an act that takes its maker's time (`publish/venue_decision` 30 minutes, `publish/tribunal_order` 45), and the next waits its turn on their timeline. 9 entries.

Times to decide support payments, median days, before then after: au-vic 6.0 to 0.0, gb-eng 0 (p90 14.5) to 0. The wrong-refusal rate itself stays until F7 (`slip()`).
  - *The clerk's "at most one paper a day"* (3 entries): the clerk keeps the books on a daily round (`CLERK_ROUND_DAYS`), which is the rhythm the plan's table says to keep ("kept as the clerk's routine"); the literal count is gone, and each paper is a person's act that takes the clerk's time. (A first version that filed on the cadence wake only left the lending office's code acting on 12 of 145 loan applications before its clerk's paper named them.)
  - *Free paperwork:* rows in the world's table for the returns (30 minutes), payroll notices (5), lending decisions (30), loan terms (15) and written approvals (5), each a placeholder that says so, and `standing-work.md` no longer says clerks cost nothing in hours. The seven unpriced offices come out of the inventory. Not done: `by` naming performers from an office's roster (the staff post's holder is the performer, and `by` stays for an actor that is not one).

## 2026-10-16 · Foundations F7 and F11, and the twins exact again (kernel, contract, participants, generator; no model called)

Three pieces, one commit each: the twins (`b7cc750`), F7 (`6de312d`), F11 (this commit). Plan: `docs/design/foundations.md` (rows F7 and F11; law 5 and law 7). Contracts: `contracts/README.md`, "Changes since v0.8 closed (2026-10-16: foundations, steps F7 and F11 ...)".

- **Twins exact again.** The cause F6 traced was right and general: an `advance` carries the clock to the next wake, and news noted after it is met *there*, so a sleeper's injury was met at whichever unit woke next, and in a town with a model's seat that unit sits at other hours than in its code twin. New log command `advance_to_news` (`Command::AdvanceToNews`): it advances as `advance` does but stops at the moment a person's body gives news (a condition begun, ended or treated; flooded out), after all that is scheduled for that moment; the engine's `next` uses it, `advance` is unchanged. A year of the twin test: acts 122,756 of 122,756, draws 74,865 of 74,865, decisions 39,979 of 39,979 alike, and `twin-draws.test.ts` is back to `expect(acted.apart).toEqual([])` (F6 allowed one in 10,000). Kernel test: an advance to news stops where the news is and reaches the same state hash as a plain advance. Not done: records and messages made by a scheduled item that no unit waits on (a visit's end, a birth) are still met at the next wake; F11's own answers needed the same stop (below) and are covered. The twin test found this twice in this work: it is the right backstop.
- **F7: `slip()`, the one way to draw an error.** `participants/src/slip.ts`: `slip(ctx, task, caseKey, {days, lean})` reads the row for the task and the kind of performer (person or system) in the world's new `orchestration.slip` table, scales it by the friction dial where the row says so, and draws from a stream named for who, what and the case; no row, no slip. Four rates moved from module parameters to rows, each with the profile's note as its source (`sources`): a wrong refusal of a claim (`publish/benefit_decision`, `frictions.support.wrong_refusal_bps`, FITTED to the first profile's survey share, scaled by place), a venue finding for an applicant with nothing to show (`publish/venue_decision`, `uphold_without_proof_bps`, a PLACEHOLDER 5,000), a wrong metered bill (`publish/invoice/metered_bill`, per year of exposure, `per_adult_bps_per_year.bill`, from the World Justice Project survey, halved), pay come short (`transfer/wages`, per year, the same survey's wages share over the town's count of exposed jobs). Gone: the parameters `error_bps`, `uphold_bps`, `billing_error_bps_per_year`, `short_pay.per_year_bps`, the `uphold-`, `bill-error-`, `short-pay-` and `claim-error-` streams, the four inventory entries; the F7 law test is on and now also holds that no module is handed a rate of error as a parameter. **Seven entries are left in the inventory: F8 six, history one.** *A fault found and mended in my own first version:* the table was written for people only (a system's rate has no source), and the support agency of the outside world is a system, so its wrong refusals went from 40 a year to none in a 1,000-person au-vic town; the three rows that are of an office's decisions (a claim, a case, a bill) are now written for systems too, with the same rate and a source line saying the figure is the office's (none for software alone was found), and the count is back (40, 43 after).
- **F11: a keeper's answer takes the keeper's time.** A look through a channel of `way: ask` onto a register whose keeper (`of`) has posts held by someone who can answer, with a row for it in the work table (`answer/<channel>`, else `answer`; seconds; a placeholder in the generator: ten minutes for a person, two seconds for a system), is put to the keeper's performer: of the holders of its posts, the one done soonest, on their own timeline (`oikos_time::place`), so one clerk answers one question at a time and a system in its seconds. `ask_started` and `ask_answered` are logged; the answer is looked through as the register is *then* and comes with the asker's next observation, once. The look that asked comes back without that channel and the observation says so: `asking` lists the channels with a question out. An office (a position's capacity) that asked is woken when the answer is done, and the advance stops at that moment (as for body news); a person asking for themselves is not woken. With no row, or nobody to answer, a question is answered at once, as before. The platform's `stepper` does not plan while a question is out (it carries its follow-ups and waits), so a module that asks a register before it judges, as the builder and the inspectors do, goes on from the answer. Tests: `kernel/tests/knowing.rs` (no row: at once; a system's two minutes; two systems answer two questions together and a third waits; one clerk answers one at a time; an advance stops at an answer), a scheduler unit test, `orchestrator/test/keepers-answers.test.ts` (a generated town: ten minutes, the registry's officers, not overlapping). In a year of the 1,000-person town: 330 questions in au-vic, 340 in gb-eng, 260 in ke-nakuru; the wait from asking to the answer is a median 3.6 hours, a p90 of 20 hours, at most 24.5 (au-vic; gb-eng 3.5, 21, 24; ke-nakuru 4.8, 19, 23), because the town's land registry has one officer, a person with a life of their own, and the first day's asks queue.
- **The support office's decision times: before F6, after F6, now.** au-vic, median days from claim to decision: **6.0** (F6's entry; the sourced processing time), **0.0** after F6, **0.0 now** (p90 0.016 days, 23 minutes). gb-eng 0 with a p90 of 14.5 before F6, 0 and a p90 of 0.006 now; ke-nakuru 0. *F11 does not bring the 6 days back, and the reason is a missing step, not a missing parameter.* Deciding a claim is the office's staff's time (a decision, 20 minutes in the table) on a claim that arrives with everything the decision reads (the law's conditions, the claimant's own figures); nothing in a claim's processing asks a keeper anything, so there is no answer to wait for, and the office has no queue of work that is not the town's. The real agency's six days are (1) a queue of the whole country's claims of which the town sends a few hundred a year, (2) evidence the claimant sends later and papers other offices confirm (identity, the income an employer reported, a separation certificate), and (3) a decision made by someone with other claims first. **Gap, named and not patched:** a law that says what a decision on a claim waits for (a paper from the claimant within so many days, a confirmation from a keeper) and an office that asks for it; then F11 makes the wait the keeper's time and the claimant's. The same holds for the other offices: desks and the tribunal keep their statutory days (14, 49 and 42), the bank's lending, planning and the letting offices are minutes to hours.
- **Measured** (`worlds/town-1000.yaml`, the living flags of the culture batches, a year, three seeds of one town each, before = `4928f1e` (F6's merge), after = this commit; `oikos diff`, `oikos health`; nothing tuned back). Beyond three standard errors: au-vic 0 of 57 measures, gb-eng 3 (departures 139 to 146, people who left the world 149.7 to 160, working age 513.7 to 509.3; the first two are one measure counted twice), ke-nakuru 3 (move-ins 59 to 80.7, leases 21.3 to 28.3, the share of renters paying over 30% of income 87.6 to 82.6). Health breaches: au-vic 5 then 4 (the change in religious affiliation is inside its tolerance now), gb-eng 5 then 5, ke-nakuru 2 then 3 (the participation rate is just over its tolerance). ## 2026-10-16 · Foundations F8: law as data, what a decision waits for and how it is reviewed (participants, generator, profiles; no kernel; no model called)

Plan: `docs/design/foundations.md` (row F8; laws 5 and 6). The behaviour is in `docs/behaviour/decisions.md`; the contract notes in `contracts/README.md` ("Changes since v0.8 closed (2026-10-16 ... step F8"). Nothing in the kernel or the JSON Schemas changed: the new things are statement kinds, the content of a law, and a profile's data.

- **The routes are a profile's data.** Each of the nine profiles states `values.decisions`: a list of rules, each for a kind of decision (and, where the place's law differs by payment, for named payments): `needs` (papers from the claimant, a confirmation from their last employer, within so many days, and what comes of it if they do not come: refuse or decide on what is on hand), `review` (the office looks at its decision again if asked within so many days; whether an appeal lies only after it), `appeal` (the matter a venue that can set aside hears; within so many days; grounds; fee in hours of pay) and `refused_by`. The generator publishes them as the higher government's law `law-decisions`. Every figure has a source line; **all are recalled and none opened**, each saying so and "(to confirm)", with the days that are only mine marked PLACEHOLDER. How sure, in `docs/behaviour/decisions.md`: medium for au-vic (review 91 days, required; Administrative Review Tribunal 91, free), gb-eng (mandatory reconsideration 30, then First-tier Tribunal 30, free), us-oh (reconsideration 65 then judge 65; Ohio unemployment 21 and 21), de-ni (Widerspruch 30 then social court 30, free) and jp-akita (an examiner apart from the office, 3 months, no review first), br-mg for the pension (30 days to the board of appeals); low for mx-jal, ke-nakuru, in-tn and br-mg's cash transfer (placeholders or analogies). Every profile also has a planning permit rule (a 30-day second look), a placeholder.
- **What a decision waits for (the missing law F7 named).** A support claim is no longer decided in the minute it is seen. The office asks, once each and as acts of its own with their time, for what the law says: the claimant's papers (a letter, `evidence_request`; the claimant sends `evidence`, naming their last employer), and for an unemployed claimant in au-vic, us-oh, de-ni and jp-akita the last employer's confirmation (`confirmation_request`; the employer's payroll office answers from its own books, `confirmation_answer`). The claim stays on the office's file while something is out and not late; at the next round it is decided when all has come, or when a need's days have run (refuse, or decide on what is on hand, as the law says). **No delay is a parameter**: the days are a deadline. The claimant, the employer's payroll unit and the office's round make the time. *New papers a seat would need a form for:* `evidence` (a claimant's papers), `confirmation_answer` (an employer's answer), `review_request` (it had a code-only kind, `remedy_request`; the one request every grievance uses, now renamed). The office's own papers (`evidence_request`, `confirmation_request`, `decision_review`) are its own forms to issue. No translator file was touched; the translator would have to know `evidence` and `review_request` before a seat in a claimant's chair could use them.
- **A decision looked at again.** `Reconsiderations` (a general class: an office, the kinds of its decisions, and its own `redo`) answers a `review_request` that is about one of its decisions of a kind with a review route: inside the law's days it decides again on the facts then on file, without a slip, records what it found (`decision_review`: outcome `changed` / `upheld` / `out_of_time`; author and time are who and when) and answers the asker (`remedy_answer`); found wrong, the office puts it right itself (the support office writes the new `benefit_decision` with `on_review` and starts paying; the planning office a new `permit_decision` and the liberty to build). A venue that sets a refusal aside is obeyed the same way (`decideAgain`). What was a memory (the support office's `wronglyRefused` and `reviewed` sets, F7's note (c)) is gone: the review recomputes the decision from the claim, and the review record is the file's. *About "a record that a decision went wrong by a slip":* the world has none, on purpose: the performer did not know it had slipped, and a record visible to the office would be visible to a seat in it. The draw is in the log (`slip-publish/benefit_decision-...`), and the world's record of the error is the review's finding.
- **Appeal.** The tribunal hears `claim_refused` (and can set aside) only where the law has an appeal for it, at the law's fee: it publishes one notice of what it hears for each fee (`hearingNotices`). A venue that can order reads the days from the law and turns away an application out of time, or without the review the law makes come first (`rejected`, with the days). The citizen's side reads the same law: it asks the office only inside the review's days, goes straight to a venue where the place has no review, and applies only inside the appeal's. Planning has a review route; no appeal is built, since nobody in the town brings a permit to a venue.
- **The three code-held rules of law 6 moved to data, and the six inventory entries are gone** (`orchestrator/test/fixtures/foundations-inventory.json`: nothing but history is left; the F8 law tests are on: three new in `foundations-laws.test.ts`). (1) *Who approves a payment over a sum*: the payments procedure carries `data.approval` (`by`, `over`); the finance office (`government.ts`, and the seat's books in `openbooks-townhall.ts`) reads it there; `approval_over` and `mayor_position` are no longer parameters. (2) *Who refuses a claim where the office is a head and staff*: the decisions law's `refused_by` (every profile: the head alone); the staff put a claim that fails before the head only where the law says so. (3) *Who carries out a removal*: the law on possession's `enforced_by`, read by the citizen (`enforcerOfRemovals`). (4) `remedy_request` as a special kind: now `review_request` in the generator, the modules, the measure query, the manifests and the tests.
- **Measured** (`worlds/town-1000.yaml`, the living flags of the culture batches, a year, three seeds of one town each, before = `ef777e5` (F7's merge), after = this change; `oikos diff`, `oikos health`; nothing tuned back).
